who_can_apply: Urban youth in Beacon. The page does not list exact ages or other rules.
how_to_apply: Watch the program's Facebook page for the application. Questions: 845-831-4287.
notes: Ages and pay are not on the page, so ask first. Program site: Beacon Recreation Center, 23 West Center Street, Beacon.
duration: Hired three times a year: spring, summer and fall
pay_detail: Paid. The wage is not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 17 for the whole program. Students must graduate high school in 2027 or 2028 (2026 page). Needs three recommenders: an English teacher, a business or social studies teacher, and a counselor.
how_to_apply: Fill out the survey to see if you qualify. Name three people to write you a recommendation. Then send the application with a resume, a one-page essay and a 3-minute pitch video. Questions: gesummer@lehigh.edu.
notes: Costs a lot. Ask about aid early since priority aid deadline was in February. Residential, no early departure.
duration: 3 weeks (2026: July 5 to 25)
pay_detail: $7,000 program fee (2026) covering tuition, room and board. Limited need-based aid for priority applicants.

who_can_apply: Teens enrolled in a Boston Public School, or who live in Boston (night, day, homeschool or GED programs count). You must be authorized to work in the US. No art experience needed. No age range is listed.
how_to_apply: Apply online, then interview with the Teen Interview Team. First come, first served. Accepted teens do onboarding and work paperwork, then Foundation Studio, then start paid work. After two interview invitations you must reapply to be contacted again.
notes: Studio at 100 W. 2nd Street, Boston, MA 02127, phone 617-268-7620. Photography, 3D design, creative technology, animation and video are Boston only. AFH also has a Brooklyn site with different rules. Work permit rule not checked.
duration: School year: Tue to Thu, 3:00 to 6:00 p.m. Summer: Mon to Thu, 11:00 a.m. to 5:15 p.m.
pay_detail: Rate not posted. Paid work starts after the first 36 Foundation Studio hours, which are unpaid.

who_can_apply: Boston youth who are 13 years old. You need proof of Boston residency (for example a Boston Public Schools report card or a landline, gas, cable or electric bill).
how_to_apply: Registration and the waitlist are closed for 2026. Watch the BCYF page for 2027 dates. When it opens, register through BCYF and show proof of Boston residency. Questions: Kate Hennigan, kate.hennigan@boston.gov, 617-961-6946.
notes: Only for 13 year olds. The page says 14 year olds looking for jobs should use the Office of Youth Employment and Opportunity page. The 2026 program has reached capacity.
duration: Six weeks, July and August
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students age 15 and up, based on the age filter on the Berklee summer page. Check the page for any playing experience needed.
how_to_apply: Use the Admissions and How to Enroll links on the Berklee summer programs page.
notes: Costs money. The year of the listed dates is not shown, so confirm dates, prices and any audition steps on the page.
duration: 5 weeks (listed dates July 9 to August 13; year not shown on the page)
pay_detail: Listed tuition $5,430, or $5,230 if you save before Jan 31. Housing $4,200. Scholarships exist (see the Scholarships link on the summer page).

who_can_apply: Boston Public School high school students who need more support go first. You must be referred. You cannot apply on your own.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's Private Industry Council (PIC) contact. You can also ask a partner group: ABCD, Boys and Girls Club of Boston, Roxbury Tenants at Harvard, Sociedad Latina or METCO. They send students in.
notes: You cannot apply directly. Talk to your school's PIC career specialist or one of the partner organizations.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Thursday, 32 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid internship; hourly rate not stated

who_can_apply: High school students entering their junior or senior year who can commit to the full 8 weeks. Boston Public School students got the first application window. Preference goes to Boston residents.
how_to_apply: The 2026 application opened January 21 for Boston Public School students and March 6 for all students. 2027 dates are not posted. The program talks only with you. It does not talk with family or teachers. Questions: juniorsummervolunteerprogram@bmc.org.
notes: In 2026 the form closed March 9 after 100 applications. That was three days after it opened to all students. The page says the program takes 70 students.
duration: 8 weeks (2026: June 29 to Aug 21)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teen members of Boys & Girls Clubs of Boston, which serves ages 6 to 18 at clubs in Boston and Chelsea. The page gives no age rule for the workforce program itself.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how teens are placed. Find your nearest Club on the Find Your Club page and ask about the Ready to Work program and the Club's Employment Specialist. General contact page: bgcb.org/contact-us.
notes: Confirm first: ages, hours and how to apply are not on the page. Under Massachusetts law (M.G.L. c.149 s.86) a child employed needs a work permit from the superintendent of schools, so ask the Club how permits are handled. The Clubs' home page said membership fees were waived for the 2025 to 2026 school year; ask about this year's fee. Teen centers: Mildred C. Hailey Teen Center (Jamaica Plain) and Josh Kraft Mattapan Teen Center. See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Rate not posted. The page says the internships are paid. The Clubs report about 500 teen jobs and internships a year.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Email volunteer@bpl.org or call 617-859-2304 to ask about openings and apply.
notes: Sites: Brighton, Central Library, Teen Central, Codman Square, East Boston, Grove Hall, Hyde Park, Mattapan, Roslindale, Shaw-Roxbury and West Roxbury. Workshops include resume building, privacy training and know your rights in the workplace.
duration: Fall (September to December) and spring (January to June) cycles; five skill workshops on Monday afternoons at 4 p.m. on Zoom
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Students who start their junior or senior year in fall 2027. Students from other countries can apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Academic Immersion page. See the How to Apply page after Dec 17.
notes: Costs money. The 2027 price is not posted yet. The course page does not say whether it gives college credit.
duration: 3 weeks. 2027 dates (pending approval): June 27 to July 16 or July 18 to Aug 6
pay_detail: 2026 total was $5,991 for commuters and $7,875 for residential students. 2027 rates post Dec 17.

who_can_apply: Students entering their junior or senior year of high school in fall 2027. Juniors need to be in Honors and/or AP courses.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application with transcript, a 500 to 750 word personal statement and one academic teacher recommendation. The student must apply, not a parent or counselor.
notes: Expensive. 2027 dates are pending approval and may change. Standardized test scores are optional for summer 2027. Contact: summerhs@bu.edu.
duration: 6 weeks; 2027 dates pending approval: June 27 to August 6, 2027
pay_detail: Summer 2026 total was $7,245 (commuter, 8 credits) or $11,565 (residential, 8 credits), plus a $75 application fee. Summer 2027 costs post December 17, 2026. Limited financial aid (need and merit).

who_can_apply: Students currently in their junior year of high school. The page says RISE is for a "domestic student" and does not define that term. Strong grades (the page says most competitive applicants are A- to A) and a STEM recommendation.
how_to_apply: You apply online yourself. Send your transcript and three short essays. Send one letter from a STEM teacher, counselor or research boss. For internships, also name three BU teachers you want to work with.
notes: Costs money. Test scores are optional for 2027. Placement in a requested lab is not guaranteed.
duration: 6 weeks (2027: June 27 to Aug 6)
pay_detail: 2026 total was $6,415 for commuters and $10,735 for residential students; $75 application fee. 2027 rates post Dec 17. Limited financial aid.

who_can_apply: Students who start sophomore, junior or senior year in fall 2027. BU looks at your grades, courses and a personal essay. Students from other countries can apply.
how_to_apply: You apply online yourself. Send a transcript that starts in 9th grade. Write a personal essay of 500 to 750 words. Pay the $75 fee.
notes: Costs money. The calendar says dates are pending approval.
duration: 2 weeks. Dates listed (pending approval): Session 1 June 20 to July 2, Session 2 July 11 to 23, Session 3 July 25 to Aug 6
pay_detail: 2026 total was $3,989 for commuters and $5,245 for residential students; $75 application fee. 2027 rates post Dec 17.

who_can_apply: Cambridge residents who are 14 through the summer after finishing high school and eligible to work in the U.S. Priority goes to students eligible for free or reduced lunch and lower-income families.
how_to_apply: Apply online through Trax, the Department of Human Service Programs enrollment system. All applications go on a waitlist for review, which does not mean the program is full. Staff then schedule hiring paperwork (original ID and Social Security card needed).
notes: Questions: youthemployment@cambridgema.gov. The page does not mention a work permit; Massachusetts requires one for workers under 18 (M.G.L. c.149 s.86; Boston youth worker rights page written with the state Attorney General's Office). Participants may not miss more than 5 program days. There is no fixed maximum age on the page; eligibility ends after the summer following high school graduation.
duration: 6 weeks, 20 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid minimum wage by the City; the page says $15.00 per hour for Summer 2025 (the page has not been updated with a 2026 rate)

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 19. Boston sites are in the Warren Gardens area of Roxbury and the Howard-Dacia area of Dorchester.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Boston Youth Job Interest Form on the Youth Employment page, or use the Apply to work as a Youth Organizer link on the Boston page.
notes: Also on the Boston page: Teen Empowerment Studios, a youth-run music and performance arts group, with its own application link. Another program, Visions for the Future, is for ages 17 to 24. Hiring dates are not posted, so ask TE.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: The site says TE employs youth. Pay rate not stated.

who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Massachusetts Wing site lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: The squadron page does not describe a visit process. Use the Contact Us and Join CAP pages on the Massachusetts Wing site. The wing phone is 781-225-6540 and its email is hq@mawg.cap.gov (these are the wing's, not the squadron's).
notes: The Massachusetts Wing also lists a Hanscom squadron (MA-043). The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.
duration: The squadron meets Saturdays from 4 to 6:30 p.m. at the Barnes Army Reserve Center, 495 Summer St., Boston, MA 02210.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 to 19 years old at the start of the internship, with a sincere interest in wildlife, education and environmental justice. About 6 to 8 interns are accepted.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application by December 9. Some applicants are invited to an in-person group interview. Email Ana Shapiro, Youth Programs Manager, at ashapiro@zoonewengland.org (no phone calls).
notes: Unpaid, so the work permit question is left open. Spring and summer teen internships are also planned; the page links a calendar of internship periods. The fall internship application is closed.
duration: 30 hours of weekend and February vacation week shifts, plus workshops
pay_detail: Unpaid internship

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18. Paid ZooTeen roles are only for teens who live in Boston and Cambridge; volunteer roles are also offered.
how_to_apply: The page does not give application steps. The school-year ZooTeen page lists the Youth Programs Manager, Ana Shapiro, at ashapiro@zoonewengland.org for questions, and an interest form for application updates.
notes: Work permit flag applies to the paid roles only (state rule: M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page, written with the Attorney General's Office); volunteers do not need one. Dates and pay were not on the page, so confirm with the zoo.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Paid roles (Boston and Cambridge residents only) and volunteer roles; hourly rate not stated

who_can_apply: Youth jobs are for ages 14 to 18 (leader jobs for 19 to 24). Must be 14 by the start of the job, have finished 6th grade, and be legally permitted to work in the U.S. Most opportunities are limited to full-time Boston residents; some have extra requirements.
how_to_apply: Browse the futureBOS catalog, apply to at least three jobs, then get an offer and finish onboarding (work permit if under 18, proof of identity and work authorization, proof of school enrollment). City of Boston agency jobs can be onboarded in one visit to the YEO office at 1483 Tremont Street.
notes: Questions: futurebos@boston.gov or 617-635-4202. Under-18 workers need a Massachusetts work permit for the specific job (a doctor must sign for ages 14 and 15); the city page explains the steps. The $15 rate is quoted from the city FAQ. The state minimum wage statute (M.G.L. c.151 s.1) says a wage of less than $15.00 per hour is presumed oppressive and unreasonable; the current 2026 minimum wage page from the state Department of Labor Standards could not be read (403), so confirm the rate in your job offer. The work permit rule is M.G.L. c.149 s.86.
duration: Summer 2026 ran June 23 to August 29. School-year jobs are limited to up to 8 hours a week for youth; summer up to 25 hours a week.
pay_detail: Youth jobs (ages 14 to 18) are paid $15 an hour; leader jobs (19 to 24) $20 an hour. Professional development programs pay a stipend.

who_can_apply: Public school students who are in 9th grade now in Boston, Cambridge or Somerville and are nominated by a principal, teacher or guidance counselor. Cohorts are 30 to 40 students.
how_to_apply: You must be nominated by a principal, teacher or counselor who knows you. Ask your school staff. Email crimsonsummer@harvard.edu for questions.
notes: Only for public school 9th graders in Boston, Cambridge and Somerville. Other nomination steps and dates are not on the page, so ask the academy. The page also mentions sophomore-year needs in its curriculum, which does not match the 9th grade rule.
duration: 3 summers (summer one is on campus, summer two is 6 weeks, summer three is the 7-week Harvard Summer School)
pay_detail: Full tuition, room and board. $800 stipend the first summer, $200 per week in summers two and three. $3,000 college scholarship after finishing all three summers.

who_can_apply: High school students who will graduate and enter college in 2027, 2028 or 2029. You must be at least 16 by June 13, 2027. You must not turn 19 before July 31, 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply online at Harvard Summer School when the application opens December 1, 2026. Financial aid is requested during the application.
notes: Expensive and selective. Residential financial aid is limited to U.S. citizens and permanent residents.
duration: 4 weeks (June 14 to July 8 or July 12 to August 5, 2027) or 7 weeks (June 21 to August 6, 2027)
pay_detail: 2027 cost $4,180 to $15,980 depending on format and length, plus a $75 application fee. Financial aid is available.

who_can_apply: Youth in grades 8 to 12. The page lists no residency rule.
how_to_apply: Use the APPLY NOW link on the Jovenes en Accion page of the Hyde Square Task Force site.
notes: The page gives no pay, residency rule or dates. Ask the Hyde Square Task Force before you apply.
duration: Year-round
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens of all skill levels and interests. The page does not give an age range, grades or a residency rule. Admission to the ICA is free for anyone 18 and under.
how_to_apply: Email teens@icaboston.org to get involved. The Teen Arts Council and Teen Exhibitions pages mention an application, but the programs page does not explain how to submit it. Phone: 617-478-3100.
notes: Confirm first. Ages, pay amount and deadlines are not on the program pages. Boston Public School students from participating high schools can earn school credit for taking part. Other ICA teen programs had no dates set. They are the Teen Digital Cooperative, and the music and photo break intensives. The page does not say whether a work permit applies.
duration: 2026 to 27 school year groups meet after school (4 to 7 p.m.; Teen Arts Council and Teen Exhibitions start at 4:30). Examples: Teen Arts Council Thursdays, Sept 10 to May 20; Fast Forward Wednesdays and Fridays, Oct 21 to May 5.
pay_detail: Participants receive compensation. The amount is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Sophomores at the Edward M. Kennedy Academy for Health Careers, Revere High School, Chelsea High School or any Boston public school. A 3.0 GPA is required to apply.
how_to_apply: Ask your school guidance counselor (or PIC career specialist) in the fall and watch the page for the spring application link. For summer jobs, contact your school's PIC career specialist.
notes: Combines the old Mass General Youth Scholars and Brigham Student Success Jobs programs. Sites include Mass General Hospital, Brigham and Women's, Faulkner Hospital and Mass Eye and Ear. Paid jobs under 18 need a Massachusetts work permit (state rule: M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page; not on the MGB page).
duration: Multi-year: exploration in 10th grade, paid internships in 11th and 12th grade
pay_detail: Paid internships in 11th and 12th grade and paid summer jobs (hourly rate not stated)

who_can_apply: Boston youth. The page does not list an age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Interest Form on the Mayor's Youth Council page. Questions: myc@boston.gov or 617-961-6980.
notes: The page does not give pay, exact ages or the next application window. Call or email the office to ask.
duration: A yearly cohort (the 2025-26 cohort was announced in December 2025)
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 10, 11 or 12 who are City of Boston residents or attend Boston Public Schools, and who can attend Thursday sessions 4 to 6:30 p.m. all year.
how_to_apply: Check the MFA Teen Programs page for the next application. This cycle's application is closed.
notes: Paid job, so teens under 18 need a Massachusetts work permit (not mentioned on the MFA page; see M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page). The MFA also offers Teen Studio Art Classes for ages 12 to 17.
duration: Thursdays 4 to 6:30 p.m., October 15, 2026 to May 27, 2027 (2026-27 cycle), plus two of three Sunday events
pay_detail: $15 per hour

who_can_apply: High school students (grades 9 to 12) interested in math or cyber security. US citizens and permanent residents.
how_to_apply: Apply online by the deadline and have a teacher recommendation sent in.
notes: The 2025 workshop was held at MIT Beaver Works. The page does not state the 2026 location. Ask before you plan travel.
duration: 1 week (2026: Aug 3 to 7)
pay_detail: Free. Not residential: you must arrange your own housing and transportation.

who_can_apply: High school students completing their junior year who are US citizens. Permanent residents who are not citizens are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Apply online by the deadline and have recommendations sent in. Contact details are on the page.
notes: The 2026 workshop ran July 12 to 25. Applications for 2026 are closed. The page does not mention when the 2027 application opens.
duration: 2 weeks (2026: July 12 to 25), living in MIT dorms
pay_detail: Free. Students pay only their own travel to and from MIT. Housing is in MIT dorms. Transport to Lincoln Lab is provided.

who_can_apply: Public school students from Boston, Cambridge or Lawrence, MA in 7th, 8th, 9th or 10th grade who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents (green card). Exceptions are not made.
how_to_apply: Create a profile in the MITES application portal and submit the MITES Saturdays application (separate from the Summer and Semester application).
notes: Students are expected to keep A and B grades; no minimum GPA to apply. The program encourages applicants who are underrepresented in STEM or from lower-income families or the first in their family to attend college.
duration: 8 Saturdays in spring and 8 in fall, 10:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., for up to about five and a half years
pay_detail: Free of charge. Students pay only their own transportation to MIT (Lawrence students get free transport).

who_can_apply: High school juniors who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents with a current green card. You can be from anywhere in the country, at a public, private or homeschool.
how_to_apply: Create a profile in the MITES application portal. MITES Summer and MITES Semester (a six-month STEM experience for rising seniors) share one application. Short-answer responses and recommendations from recent teachers are needed.
notes: Competitive and focused on students from underserved or under-resourced backgrounds. Residential on campus.
duration: Six weeks, late June through early August, weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
pay_detail: Free of charge. Students pay only for transportation; travel scholarships are available for MITES Summer.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores and juniors who live in the US, including homeschooled students. If you live near Boston, you meet mentors on campus and use the main application. If you live farther away, you use a separate application called PRIMES-USA and meet mentors by video or phone. Students outside the US can join CrowdMath instead.
how_to_apply: Use the online application portal linked on the MIT PRIMES how to apply page. It has an online questionnaire. It asks for two or three recommenders. Math teachers or camp counselors are ideal. It asks for a personal statement of up to 2 pages. It asks for lists of math books, courses, camps and computing skills. It also asks for solutions to the PRIMES 2027 Math Problem Set. Apply if you solve at least 70 percent. Upload solutions as one PDF with your name only in the file name.
notes: Competitive and heavy on math. There is also PRIMES Circle, a spring math enrichment program. It is for students within commuting distance of Boston. It has its own apply page at https://math.mit.edu/research/highschool/primes/circle/apply-circle.html, which was not read. Phone: (617) 253-4381.
duration: A year long after school program. The start date is not stated.
pay_detail: Free to join. Pay is not mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Students now in 11th grade with a permanent family address in the US and little or no engineering experience. About 20 spots, and the page says it generally gets over 300 applications. Students should not have completed WTP curriculum coursework or WTP summer programs.
how_to_apply: Online SlideRoom application: three personal essays, and online forms from one math teacher and one science teacher.
notes: You cannot apply in earlier grades. Students should not plan another job or internship during the four weeks. Students outside the US are not eligible.
duration: 4 weeks, June 26 to July 24, 2027, residential
pay_detail: Free to apply. Free to attend if family income is $120,000 or less. Otherwise $2,000 ($120,000 to $150,000), $4,000, $8,000 or $20,000 by income. Housing and food included. More aid may be asked for.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 19. You must be in high school or an equivalent program.
how_to_apply: Watch the museum's internship job board. Use View Internships on the Museum of Science internships page. Apply to the youth internship posting when it opens.
notes: The museum pages do not say if the internships are paid, so ask before you apply. Massachusetts law (M.G.L. c.149 s.86) says a child needs a work permit from the superintendent of schools to be employed. The museum also has Youth Volunteers, ages 14 to 19 and in high school. The volunteer page gives no application steps beyond a general interest form. See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.
duration: The summer program is 7 weeks. The academic year program runs during the school year. Hours are not stated.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the museum pages.

who_can_apply: People ages 14 to 19 who are in high school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the volunteer page. It asks for your name, contact details, birthdate, address, what interests you and when you are free.
notes: The page gives few details for youth roles and does not say whether any roles are paid. Ask what is open.
duration: Not stated for youth volunteers (Classic adult volunteers sign up for a 4 month commitment)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 and older. Most internships are open to residents of Boston and Cambridge.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application opens (expected next March). Interns also attend a weekly professional development course and an ocean advocacy course. Questions: teens@neaq.org.
notes: Paid job, so teens under 18 need a Massachusetts work permit (the aquarium page does not mention it; M.G.L. c.149 s.86 and the Boston youth worker rights page, written with the state Attorney General's Office, cover the permit rule). The aquarium also runs ClimaTeens (ages 13 and up, 2026-27 applications due October 18, 2026).
duration: One week of training and six weeks of work
pay_detail: All teen internships are paid positions (rate not stated)

who_can_apply: Rising juniors and seniors in high school. The page does not say whether US and international students are both eligible. London program students must be 17 or older by the start of the program. No minimum age is listed for Boston or Oakland.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application. Add an unofficial high school transcript or report card. Add a personal statement of up to 250 words. A teacher or counselor reference is optional. You ask for financial aid inside the application.
notes: Expensive. The page names Summer 2027 programs in Boston, London and Oakland. Session dates were not posted. For a free Northeastern option for Massachusetts juniors see the Young Scholars Program card.
duration: Twelve days, move in on Sunday and move out the following Friday. Summer 2027 session dates were not posted on the program pages.
pay_detail: Summer 2027 tuition is $6,995 and includes tuition, course materials, housing, meals and social activities. Need based financial aid is available, and a non-refundable deposit of 20 percent of tuition (after aid and discounts) holds your spot. Priority round applicants get a $500 discount.

who_can_apply: Current juniors. You must be a permanent Massachusetts resident. That means you live and go to school in MA all year. You must live within commuting distance of campus. You must be a US citizen or permanent resident, with no exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Online Student Application. It takes 60 to 90 minutes. You cannot save it or restart it. So write the essay answers ahead of time. You also need two teacher recommendations. A STEM teacher is best. Enter the recommenders' email addresses in the application.
notes: Free, but only for Massachusetts residents who are US citizens or permanent residents. Late applications are not accepted. Read the program FAQ before emailing the coordinator. The same page also has a line saying applications are due March 2nd, 2026, which conflicts with the March 1, 2027 close date. Confirm the 2027 date with the program before you plan around it.
duration: About six weeks. 2027 dates: June 22 to July 31, 2027, Monday to Thursday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., in person on the Northeastern campus.
pay_detail: Free program. No stipend is mentioned on the page.

who_can_apply: Must be 15 on or before the first day and not turn 19 during the program. U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident. You must live locally. You should enjoy working with kids who are 7 to 12 years old.
how_to_apply: In 2026: download the YCC application form from the park page, add 1 or 2 references, scan it and email it to npb_youthprograms@nps.gov. Applications for 2026 are closed.
notes: Paid. Mon to Fri. No housing. Work includes safety duties with young campers and training on public land management. This is a federal job, so ask the park how the Massachusetts permit rule applies. Watch the park page in early 2027. Paid work for people under 18 in Massachusetts needs a work permit (employment permit). See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 2026 schedule: Monday June 29 to Friday August 21, about 30 to 35 hours a week, 9 AM to 4 PM
pay_detail: $16.00 per hour

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 18 for the three main programs (per the Civic Engagement page).
how_to_apply: Use the application link on the Youth Employment page (school-year Youth Leader program).
notes: The page does not state pay, dates or deadlines. Confirm pay and current dates with Sociedad Latina.
duration: School-year after-school plus summer
pay_detail: Listed on the Youth Employment page. Pay amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Boston youth ages 14 to 25.
how_to_apply: Sign up for the newsletter or follow @oyeaboston to be notified when the next voting cycle opens. Contact ylc@boston.gov or 617-961-6980.
notes: The page calls it the first youth-focused participatory budgeting initiative in the United States.
duration: Yearly cycle: ideas, proposals, voting, then projects built
pay_detail: Not a job. Youth take part in the civic process.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10-12 at a NYC high school, with a parent's signed consent, available 3 to 6 hours a week outside school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application or mail a print application to the Librarians of Tomorrow Internship Program, 10 Grand Army Plaza, Brooklyn, NY 11238. Questions: LOT@bklynlibrary.org or 718-230-2406.
notes: Library teen page lists ages 15-18; the page requires grades 10-12 in NYC. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Nov 2026 to June 2027, 3-6 hours a week, 100 hours total
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated), plus volunteer service hours.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10-12 at a NYC high school, with a parent's signed consent, available 3 to 5 hours a week outside school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Selected applicants are contacted for an interview. Questions: storyteen@bklynlibrary.org.
notes: Funded through the NYC Council's City's First Readers initiative. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Nov 2026 to May 2027, 3-5 hours a week, 100 hours total
pay_detail: Stipend (amount not stated), plus volunteer service hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16-19, with a parent's signed consent for 75 hours of intern service outside school, available to meet weekly.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. All applicants get an email after. Some are invited to interview.

pay_detail: Unpaid. Kindness Club gives 1 volunteer hour per meeting.

who_can_apply: The library says a volunteer is someone 16 or older who helps on a regular basis. If you are under 18, use the teen form. Call the library to ask if younger teens can apply.
how_to_apply: Download and print the teen volunteer application from the volunteering page, fill it out, and bring it to the library at 60 Livingston Ave. There is no online submission. Phone: (732) 745-5108.
notes: The teen form file name says 2018, so ask the library if it is still current. The page does not mention work permits; ask the library.
duration: Regular, ongoing help; hours not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: The Teen Advisory Board is open to Metuchen residents in grades 6 to 12. Summer volunteering is open to all teens in grades 9 to 12. In the school year, volunteering is only for grades 9 to 12. You must have volunteered in a summer or be active on the board.
how_to_apply: Use the volunteer application on the teens page. Then contact the Teen Services Librarian. Her name is on the application.
notes: Board meetings in fall 2026 are listed for Oct 20 and Nov 17 on the page.
duration: Summer volunteering runs July to August. The board meets once a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The Teen Advisory Board has a 15 hour service minimum for the year.

who_can_apply: High school age youth in Middlesex County who finished 8th grade for 9th grade entry. Students are picked by grades, a career-tech test, an interview and a counselor's note. Space is limited. County applicants are admitted first.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the district enrollment link. A parent or guardian must say yes. You can also get applications at the schools in all county towns.
notes: This is a school program, not a job. Students from outside the county are admitted only if there is space.
duration: High school years
pay_detail: No tuition for Middlesex County residents. Non-residents pay tuition set by the board.

who_can_apply: Any Middlesex County student who finished 7th grade and is going into 8th grade. You should like the idea of career and tech classes.
how_to_apply: In 2026 the page offered a waiting list form. Watch the Magnet Schools site for the 2027 sign up.
notes: For younger teens only: students must have just finished 7th grade.
duration: 12 days: July 6 to 23 in 2026, Monday to Thursday
pay_detail: Free. Students provide their own transportation.

who_can_apply: Teens in grades 6 to 12 (the library cannot accept volunteers after they turn 18). Math Tutors are grades 9 to 12; Chess Tutors are grades 8 to 12. Teen Advisory Board needs an application.
how_to_apply: Stop by the Youth Services desk to get an application. If you want to try for an Organization Club spot, write to teenvolunteers@oldbridgelibrary.org. There are not many spots.
notes: You can request a letter that confirms your volunteer hours by email.
duration: Varies by role (Math Tutors are Saturdays 11 am to 1 pm during the school year; Tech Helpers work Mondays and Saturdays, year-round)
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer credit hours.

who_can_apply: Shelvers must be going into 9th grade or older. Teen Advisory Board needs an application.
how_to_apply: Apply with the Teen Advisory Board form on the page. For volunteering, email the Teen Volunteer Coordinator and join the volunteer mailing list. Shelvers interview and train first.
notes: Selection is not first come first served.
duration: Shelvers get one 1 hour shift a week. The Teen Advisory Board meets about twice a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer hours can be confirmed.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be ages 14 and older. Teens who are younger than that cannot join.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Registration Form linked on the page.
notes: The township public safety page lists separate police volunteer options. The ages for those were not read.
duration: As needed; events are in early May, October and December
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: College-bound youth from urban communities in Atlantic, Camden, Essex, Hudson, Mercer, Middlesex, Passaic and Union counties, with a B or better GPA, top 25% of the class, and interest in volunteering to help 4-H with STEM programs.
how_to_apply: Online application on the program site (opens early in the year). About 60 students are accepted each year. Contact on the Rutgers 4-H STEM site: Chad Ripberger, ripberger@njaes.rutgers.edu.
notes: Only students in the listed counties qualify. Selected students start with an orientation in May and two short online modules.
duration: Year-round, multi-year; 2026 summer program at Rutgers-New Brunswick was July 6 to 10
pay_detail: Free: direct summer program expenses are paid by a scholarship valued at $1,000. No wage or stipend is listed.

who_can_apply: High school students entering 10th, 11th or 12th grade in the fall. Only 45 students were accepted in 2026. Applicants write a five paragraph personal response.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and write the five paragraph answer. Questions: BOLD@cinj.rutgers.edu.
notes: Two groups run it. They are the LIFE Center at Rutgers Cancer Institute and the Center for School and Community-Based Research and Education. A reunion camp is open to past campers.
duration: 1 week, 9:30 am to 4:00 pm (July 20 to 24 in 2026)
pay_detail: No application fee. Accepted students paid a non-refundable $500 enrollment fee in 2026 (due June 1, 2026).

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students. Sessions are by grade level in spring 2026: 9th graders July 20 to 24, 10th graders July 27 to 31, 11th graders July 13 to 17 (2026 dates). Open to all students of any gender.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the application steps in the text read. Check the TARGET page and the School of Engineering contact page.
notes: Program director is named on the page. Programs for grades 6 to 8 run in June and July too.
duration: 1 week, 9 am to 5 pm
pay_detail: $500 for the one-week program. Need-based sponsorship is available after acceptance. Families provide transportation.

who_can_apply: High school students finishing sophomore or junior year, ages 16 to 18. The page states this age rule for Summer 2026, so check the 2027 rules. U.S. and international students.
how_to_apply: Online application on the Pre-College Summer site. Join the email list for 2027 updates.
notes: Costs money. Check the Costs page for the current year before planning. The page did not list financial aid; ask the program. Per the Costs page for 2026: credit academies are Physical Therapy $3,784 in-state and $4,804 out-of-state, and Building Leadership Strategies $3,887.50 in-state and $5,068 out-of-state. The $500 deposit is non-refundable. No 2027 cost is posted.
duration: One week, residential
pay_detail: 2026 cost was $2,899 for most academies ($3,887.50 to $5,068 for the two credit academies), with a $500 non-refundable deposit. Includes dorm for the week.

who_can_apply: Strong high school students, from 8th graders going into 9th through 12th graders about to graduate. You need a transcript. You also need letters from your math, science or engineering teachers.
how_to_apply: Apply online with your transcript and letters from your teachers. Applications that are not complete are not reviewed.
notes: Selective program. Email the coordinator listed on the page if you need help getting a laptop.
duration: 2 weeks, 9 am to 4:30 pm (July 6 to 17 in 2026). Non-residential.
pay_detail: $875 for the two-week session.

who_can_apply: Current high school students ages 16 to 18 (must be 16 by the course start date) with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA, who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Graduating seniors are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Online application plus unweighted transcript, a Parent/Guardian Permission Form and a letter of recommendation (teacher or anyone who knows your work). Reviewed first come, first served; decisions in 5 to 7 business days.
notes: Some courses need extra technology or prerequisite courses. Withdrawing after the add/drop period puts a W on a Rutgers transcript. Questions: summerscholars@rutgers.edu.
duration: Summer Session I (started May 26, 2026) or Session II (started July 6, 2026)
pay_detail: 2026 rates per credit: in-state $482 (Arts and Sciences) to $551 (SEBS), out-of-state $1,148 to $1,338, plus a one-time $162 student fee. Courses are typically 3 credits; up to two courses.

who_can_apply: Motivated high school students entering grades 10 to 12 who have completed at least one high school biology course.
how_to_apply: Online application only: about 250-word essay on your interest, high school transcripts or report cards, and your preferred session. Acceptance emails go out in the first week of April; pay within 2 weeks to hold the spot.
notes: Held at EOHSI, 170 Frelinghuysen Road, Piscataway. Questions: THED@eohsi.rutgers.edu. Expect the 2027 cycle to follow the same winter pattern, but confirm on the page.
duration: One week, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (2026 sessions: July 20 to 24 and July 27 to 31)
pay_detail: $975 non-refundable camp fee covers tuition, manuals, materials, safety equipment, lab supplies and lunch. Need-based financial aid may be available. No housing or transportation provided; no stipend.

who_can_apply: Students who finished 8th grade and are in 9th, 10th or 11th grade. You must live in and go to school in New Brunswick, Perth Amboy or Plainfield. You must be first in your family to go to college, or low income. You must be a US citizen or permanent resident. You need at least a C average and a plan to go to college. You must send an application and a personal statement, and do an interview.
how_to_apply: Email upwardbound@echo.rutgers.edu or call (848) 445-3090 to ask how to apply. The page says you fill out an application and a personal statement, and you have an interview. It shows no link to apply. Virtual open houses are held in fall in English and Spanish.
notes: Students must be willing to get to campus every day of the summer (parent ride or bus program). A separate Pre-College Outreach program is described on the same page. Checked 2026-10-10: the page names the 2027 application but shows no link to it, so apply_url stays empty.
duration: Year-round, with a six-week Summer Institute
pay_detail: Free program. The program page does not say if students get paid.

who_can_apply: Mathematically talented high school students. No specific grade or age is listed. You must submit solutions to the Problems to Explore.
how_to_apply: Four parts: Student Information and Consent Google Form (with a parent), your solutions to the Problems to Explore, a teacher recommendation emailed directly, and a transcript emailed by your counselor.
notes: Residential; students go home on weekends. The page was the Summer 2026 listing.
duration: Four weeks (2026: July 6 to 31), residential, home on weekends
pay_detail: Expected $4,800 for 2026 (tuition, materials, housing and Monday to Friday meals). Partial and need-based scholarships available.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 18 who have completed ninth grade. Weekday shifts are 4 to 6 p.m. for ages 15 and up, or 6 to 8 p.m. for ages 16 and up.
how_to_apply: Email the Volunteer Director (Jacob.Persily@rwjbh.org) with the teen's name, high school and current grade. Applications are not sent at a parent's request. Then comes orientation. Next is medical clearance. That is a health form from a doctor covering TB screening, immunizations and flu vaccine. Then a drug screen. Phone: 732-937-8507.
notes: Volunteers must be fully vaccinated and wear the provided uniform. The page says internships and shadowing are not offered. A newer and an older version of this page disagreed on hours (75 vs 100 a year); the page on 2026-10-09 says 100.
duration: Minimum 100 hours of service per year; the hospital hopes for 2 to 3 hours a week. Shifts mornings, afternoons and evenings, 7 days a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The required urine drug screen is free to the volunteer; no other costs are listed.

who_can_apply: High school students who have completed a high school level biology course. No age or grade range is stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Online application posted on the WISE page; first come, first served. Pay the fee within 2 weeks of approval.
notes: In-person sessions are non-residential at the Waksman Institute on the Busch campus in Piscataway. The year-long Waksman Student Scholars Program (WSSP) is a separate, school-based program that starts with teachers.
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Friday (2026 sessions: June 22 to July 2, July 27 to August 7; vWISE August 10 to 21)
pay_detail: $2,200 for the in-person WISE (non-refundable, due 2 weeks after approval). A virtual vWISE costs $600.

who_can_apply: Library patrons in grades 7 to 12. Book reviews are for grades 8 to 12 who live in Woodbridge. Details differ by branch.
how_to_apply: Contact the branch library. You can also write to the Teen Services team at teenservices@woodbridgelibrary.org. You can just drop in to a Community Service Club meeting.
notes: The Fords Branch Library will help you get volunteer hours for National Honor Society applications. It does this when other ways do not work.
duration: Most roles are all year, about 1 hour a week. Summer Reading Club volunteering is June to August, up to 5 hours a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn volunteer hours and signatures.

who_can_apply: 15 high school students. High school principals suggest them, one member and one backup per school. The Mayor then names them for one year starting in August. Members can apply again until they graduate.
how_to_apply: Ask your high school principal to recommend you. The Mayor then appoints members for a one-year term starting in August.
notes: Very small: about 15 seats. The page lives on a township website that uses the woodbridgelibrary.org address.
duration: One year term, August 1 to July 31
pay_detail: Not stated; this is a civic board.

who_can_apply: Youth in grades K to 13. The Rutgers 4-H homepage says it serves everyone in grades K through 13.
how_to_apply: Use the Join 4-H form on the New Jersey 4-H site, or find your county 4-H office on the Rutgers 4-H page.
notes: Not a job. It is a youth group. The Rutgers homepage has a Join 4-H form and a link to the New Jersey 4-H Camp. The pages did not give fees, so ask your county 4-H office.
duration: Ongoing clubs and programs; camp is a week in summer
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the program pages. Ask your county 4-H office.

who_can_apply: Juniors who live or go to school in New Jersey and are legal U.S. residents. You must be fluent in English and able to attend the whole session. You must be willing to take part in nondenominational prayer, patriotic ceremonies, the Pledge and the National Anthem. An Auxiliary unit must sponsor you.
how_to_apply: Contact a local American Legion Auxiliary unit or a county chairperson to ask for sponsorship. The site lists contacts. You cannot apply without a sponsor.
notes: Girls only. Start asking local Auxiliary units in the winter. The 2026 site says sponsorships were already filled. A matching program for boys (Jersey Boys State) is run by the American Legion.
duration: About 5 days (2026: Sunday June 21 to Thursday June 25)
pay_detail: No pay. Sponsors (units, posts or other groups) enroll and sponsor delegates; the site does not list a fee to the student.

who_can_apply: High school juniors with at least one semester left. Posts pick students with school help, or you can apply on your own as self-sponsored.
how_to_apply: If a post sponsors you, your school staff recommend you. The local American Legion post interviews you. If you sponsor yourself, make an account on the ALJBS CampSite portal. Fill out the questionnaire. Add a 300 to 500 word essay, or a video or a counselor reference. Pay the $50 fee.
notes: Boys only (Jersey Girls State is a separate program). Post-sponsored and self-sponsored costs are in pay_detail.
duration: One week; delegates arrive on Father's Day (the 80th session began June 21, 2026)
pay_detail: Post-sponsored: parents pay a $50 non-refundable fee and the post pays the rest. Self-sponsored: $50 non-refundable application fee plus $325 tuition if accepted (food, housing and supplies included). Scholarships may be available.

who_can_apply: Students ages 15 or older. You must give immunization records or get screened (MMR, chickenpox, TB blood test, hepatitis B, and a flu shot Dec 1 to Apr 30) and attend orientation.
how_to_apply: Online application only, then orientation and on-site training. Questions: Volunteer Services, 609-303-4023, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday to Friday.
notes: Does not offer internships or shadowing. Year-round track runs Sept 14, 2026 to June 30, 2027 when open. Check the page for when applications reopen.
duration: Summer: 7 weeks, at least 56 hours. Also 12 week seasonal and Sept to June year-round tracks.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.

who_can_apply: New Jersey residents who have finished their junior year at a public, private or home school. Applicants must be nominated by their high school (one nominee per 325 juniors). It is competitive. Fewer than 25% of nominees get offers.
how_to_apply: Get nominated by your high school, then submit the online application with essays (admission is based heavily on essays). Contact: njgset@soe.rutgers.edu or 848-445-4753.
notes: Residential at Rutgers School of Engineering, 98 Brett Road, Piscataway. The Application Instructions page on the program site still mentions the Summer 2023 application, so rely on the state page and director for 2027 dates.
duration: About 4 weeks, starting close to the beginning of July, with about 40 hours of prep work beforehand
pay_detail: Free to students and families (tuition, room and board paid by donations). FAQ says students bring a $65 key deposit returned at the end. The FAQ page is undated.

who_can_apply: Rising seniors with at least a 3.2 GPA and 95 percent attendance. Students in the MCTS Academy or Shared-Time programs cannot apply.
how_to_apply: Create an account in the MCTS online application portal and apply. Your counselor then uploads transcripts and attendance. Email admissions@mcts.edu with questions.
notes: You become a regular college student with a MyMercer account. Most classes are on the West Windsor campus. Mercer County residency is not spelled out on the page, so ask admissions. The Aviation section says that by continuing this program, costs could range from $24,000 to $36,000. The page does not say what that covers.
duration: Senior year, follows the college calendar
pay_detail: Free. No tuition for the college classes.

who_can_apply: 10th graders. Applicants are ranked by an acceptance criteria score. The page lists district information sessions, which are not required for admission. Your home district provides transportation.
how_to_apply: Create an account in the online application portal and fill in the application. Your school counselor then uploads transcripts and attendance. Email admissions@mcts.edu with questions.
notes: Students in a shared-time program cannot also do Career Prep. Ask your counselor for the deadline. Programs are at the Assunpink Center (Trenton) and the Sypek Center (Pennington).
duration: 2 years (grades 11 and 12), half day
pay_detail: Part of your regular school day. No cost stated.

who_can_apply: Students applying for the 2027-28 school year. The district serves students from Somerset and neighboring counties. Some programs (biomedical, finance, HVACR, global business) are shared-time only.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the admissions page. An admissions test may be required (see the CTE Admissions Testing page). Call Pupil Services at 908-526-8900 ext. 7250 or 7243.
notes: Health and medical sciences academy has its own admission page and phone, 908-526-8900 ext. 7148. Enrolled students can join a paid Cooperative Education job placement. That is not open to outside teens.
duration: 2027-28 school year start
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students. Ages and grades are not listed on the page. Scholarships are first come, first served, with priority to Greater Trenton Area students who attend all four weeks.
how_to_apply: Register through CampDoc and pay a 50 percent deposit. For a scholarship, fill out the separate online Financial Aid form for each child.
notes: The scholarship wording on the page still says 2025, so confirm it. Bus rides from several Trenton stops are mentioned. Contact 609-737-3735.
duration: 1 to 4 weeks, weekdays 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: $525 to $575 per week in 2026. Limited full scholarships based on financial need.

who_can_apply: Ages differ by role: 14 for Critter Care (and stream sampling with an adult), 15 for Sunday Stewardship on your own, 16 for the Welcome Desk and Butterfly House Crew.
how_to_apply: Fill in the volunteer application through the Apply Here link on the page. You get a link to log your hours after you apply. Questions: 609-737-3735.
notes: Some roles need your own ride. The page says one stream monitoring role is not a good fit for 12th graders.
duration: Varies: Sundays March to November, Tuesday mornings mid June to August, one year for animal care

who_can_apply: Young adults ages 16 to 25 who do not have a high school diploma.
how_to_apply: Send the online services request form on the NJ Department of Labor page for general questions. The state page does not list sign-up steps, so ask for the site that serves your county.
notes: For teens 16 and up who left school without a diploma. Not for students still working toward a diploma in a regular school. It includes help getting a high school equivalency diploma or an adult high school diploma. It includes counseling and help moving on to college or jobs. Paid work for people under 18 in New Jersey needs working papers (online). See permit.html?state=nj for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Full time, year-round program; length of each cohort is not stated on the state page
pay_detail: Corpsmembers get a stipend while enrolled. The amount is not stated on the state page.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 through 12. The page does not list an age rule or a residency rule; it describes students from New Jersey.
how_to_apply: Research a global issue and write a paper with a teacher or mentor, following the guidelines PDF on the page. Register and submit the paper through the World Food Prize website.
notes: The Rutgers page was read through a summarizing fetch tool because the site blocks plain page requests, so check the page itself for the 2027 date. It is listed on the New Jersey 4-H page as a program for high school students.
duration: One day (2026 date: March 6, 2026)
pay_detail: Free to take part (no registration cost). For students invited to the Global Youth Institute in Des Moines, most expenses are covered by the World Food Prize, but travel is not included.

who_can_apply: Youth from kindergarten up to age 19. A kindergartner must turn 5 by January 1 of the 4-H year. A teen cannot enroll or re-enroll if they will turn 19 before January 1 of the new club year (club year runs Oct 1 to Sept 30). Counties can set their own details.
how_to_apply: Contact your county Cornell Cooperative Extension office. Join a club. If you cannot join a club, you can enroll as an independent member. You work on projects at your own pace with an adult helping.
notes: Not a job. The rules are for New York State 4-H as described by two county Cornell Cooperative Extension pages (Jefferson and Erie). The listed URL is the Erie County page. Your own county office has the sign-up steps and costs.
duration: 4-H year runs October 1 to September 30; you can re-enroll each year
pay_detail: Fees are not stated on the program pages. Ask your county office.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.

who_can_apply: Youth 14 to 17 can go to the weeks set aside for that age. Campers must be the minimum age by December 1 of the calendar year. The pages do not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Set up a family account in the DEC online registration system. Fill out the camper forms and waivers in the Document Center before registration opens. Then register for a week and pay online. If a week is full, join the waitlist.
notes: This is a camp for campers, not a job. The main camp page still mentions a March 2025 opening, so use the How to Register page for dates. Ask DEC about sponsorships early.
duration: One week, Sunday afternoon to Friday afternoon (2026 teen weeks ran July 12 to Aug 7, depending on the camp)
pay_detail: $350 per camper per week, with meals and trips included. Transportation to and from camp is not included. Many campers are sponsored by local conservation groups, clubs and community groups.

who_can_apply: Girls. Your local American Legion Auxiliary unit picks citizens and alternates, sometimes with interviews, essays or a nomination. The pages did not list a grade or residency rule, so ask your unit.
how_to_apply: Contact your local American Legion Auxiliary unit. Ask your guidance counselor or email egsregistrar@gmail.com with your hometown, county and school. Join the local selection. Then use the login the unit gives you. Register online and pay the fee.
notes: Girls only. The site says there is a virtual orientation on Zoom in May or June. The program says it is not a sports camp or a recreational camp.
duration: One week: Sunday June 27 to Friday July 2, 2027
pay_detail: A non-refundable application fee is required. The amount is not stated on the program pages. Optional extras (shirts, survival kit) have order forms.

who_can_apply: Strong swimmers who meet the age and certification rules. Outside Long Island, the minimum age is 15 for pool posts and 16 for other posts. On Long Island the minimum is 17 (16 for pool posts only). You also need a background check, a medical form and an interview.
how_to_apply: Fill out the lifeguard job application and email it to the address on the page. Then sign up for a qualifier. Long Island has its own preregistration. After you pass, regional staff tell you the next steps.
notes: The minimum age depends on region (see who_can_apply). Confirm your age with the regional office. The New York Department of Labor page returned an access error. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Seasonal; the page says the peak operating season is May through September
pay_detail: Paid job. Candidates are in pay status during the mandatory 40 hours of training. The hourly rate is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Newark-area high school students. The page does not list grade, residency or GPA rules.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain the steps. Email explorersprogram@newarkmuseumart.org or call 973-596-5143.
notes: This is a long commitment. Ask about the 2027 application dates.
duration: 3 to 4 years: 6 after-school hours a week, 60 service hours a year, 25 hours a week in summer
pay_detail: Students are paid. The amount is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. No other rules listed.
how_to_apply: Use the registration link on the program page. For aid, use the financial aid form or contact April Jeffries at ajeffries@njpac.org.
notes: The page lists month and day but not the year, so confirm the dates before registering. Tuition is $500 for the year, with a payment plan option and aid available. Not a paid job.
duration: Fall semester Oct 3 to Dec 12 and spring semester Jan 30 to May 15, 1 to 5 pm, at 31 Mulberry Street, Newark. The page does not show the year.
pay_detail: $500 for the full year. NJPAC says no student is turned away for financial need; use the financial aid form.

who_can_apply: Any high school student in grades 9 to 12. No experience is needed. No grades, essays or recommendation letters are needed. A parent consent form is needed.
how_to_apply: Register on the ACE GNY website. Use the yellow button on the students page. Get a parent to sign a consent form. Pick a team from the map you get by email. Then wait for a confirmation email.
notes: Teams meet at host firms or universities. The page also links to a Summer Internship Program for alumni, which this card does not cover.
duration: Late October through May (about 2 hours after school per meeting). Some teams start in January.
pay_detail: Free. No pay is mentioned. Scholarship and internship chances are listed as benefits.

who_can_apply: High school seniors (12th grade) who live in one of the five boroughs. You must send a current transcript or report card that shows 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application form linked on the Apollo page. It includes an essay, a transcript or report card, and recommendations. All are due by the deadline. Late or incomplete applications are not read.
notes: The FAQ says accepted interns under 18 must give the Apollo a copy of their New York State working papers before orientation. Ask your school guidance counselor how to get working papers. The Apollo also runs a paid technical theater internship in the summer. The page text about length is not the same in two places. Confirm with the Apollo.
duration: The 2026 internship ran Apr 21 to May 21, 2026, on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays 3 to 6 PM. The page calls it six weeks in one place and eight or ten weeks in others.
pay_detail: $17.00 per hour

who_can_apply: Rising seniors going into 12th grade in September who live in the five boroughs of New York City. You like technical theater. You must come to the full program and a parent or guardian orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on Formstack before the deadline. The page says group interviews happen by appointment. Accepted teens and a parent or guardian go to an orientation on the first day.
notes: The Apollo Arts Administration internship page says interns under 18 must show New York State working papers. This technical internship page does not say so. Expect to need them for a paid job.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday, on site. The 2026 program ran July 13 to Aug 21, 2026.
pay_detail: $17 per hour

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 11 who start in Tier 1 (9th grade), Tier 2 (10th grade or Tier 1 done) or Tier 3 (11th grade or Tier 2 done). No age or borough rule is stated. You do not have to share immigration status for Tiers 1 to 3.
how_to_apply: Apply online (an account lets you save your progress). You write short answers and give references, then join a group interview. Apprentices must reapply every year. Two references use a separate online reference form.
notes: Tiers 1 to 3 are not employees. Tier 4 apprentices must be legally authorized to work and eligible under NYC Department of Labor rules, per the page. Partial participation is not allowed. Questions: gap@bbg.org (shown on the page) or 718-623-7252.
duration: 9 months, March to November 2027 (about 4 to 6 hours a week in spring and fall, 20 to 25 hours a week in summer; about 190 to 220 hours total).
pay_detail: Tier 1 $600, Tier 2 $700, Tier 3 $800 as a one-time nontaxable reimbursement in November, plus a $75 perfect attendance bonus. Tier 4 (by invitation after Tier 3) is a part-time staff job at $17 per hour. No fee to join.

who_can_apply: High school students who are U.S. citizens, permanent residents or in the U.S. for other than a temporary purpose, from a low-income household and/or first in the family to go to college. About 60 students are served each year.
how_to_apply: The Program Overview page says to click its apply link (a short link). Phone: 718-289-5855. Ask the program about this year's dates.
notes: The page says low-income means family taxable income at or below 150 percent of the poverty level. Two thirds of participants must be both low-income and first generation. One third must be one or the other. After-school tutoring runs 4:30 to 7 PM on weekdays when the host school does not offer it.
duration: Academic year: 21 Saturdays from September to April, 10 AM to 2 PM plus STEM labs 2:30 to 4:30 PM. Summer: six weeks, with three weeks as a commuter at BCC and three weeks at a residential site.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program pages. The pages do not list a cost.

who_can_apply: New York City high school students ages 14 to 19. Twelve students are chosen for each session. The page encourages you to apply again if you were not accepted before.
how_to_apply: Fill out the free online application on the Bronx Museum event page for the session. Educators read the applications and pick 12 students. If you have questions, write to education@bronxmuseum.org.
notes: The fall 2026 application form is closed, so no apply link is listed here. Check the Teen Programs page for the next one. The museum is under renovation but stays open Wednesday to Sunday, 11 AM to 6 PM, at 1040 Grand Concourse. The pages do not say whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Teen Council: two four-month sessions a year (fall and spring), twice a week after school. Fall 2026 runs late October 2026 to mid-February 2027, Mondays and Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM. Teen Summer: four weeks, three afternoons a week.
pay_detail: Teens are paid a stipend. The amount is not stated on the pages.

who_can_apply: Rising seniors at a high school in any of the five boroughs. You need an interest in the arts, a GPA of 2.0 or higher, and an unofficial transcript.
how_to_apply: Use the Enroll button on the BAM BIAC page, which links to an online form. The page lists the Education Program Manager for questions. Include an unofficial high school transcript.
notes: Only 13 spots. After the program, BAM Education alumni ages 18 to 24 can join a separate paid Creative Career Collective (virtual, Oct to Dec). Pay amount and work-permit rules are not on the page.
duration: One year in 3 sessions: one week in August (Mon to Fri, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m.), October to December, and February to June (1 to 2 days a week, 4 to 6 p.m.). The 2026-27 cohort runs Aug 2026 to Jun 2027.
pay_detail: The page says the internship is paid. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade in New York City public schools.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. It says applications usually open at the end of the school year. Check the Youth Advisory Council page or ask the Borough President's office.
notes: The council is run with the Brooklyn North and Brooklyn South high school superintendents and Sadie Nash Leadership Project. The page does not say whether members are paid or where teens must live, so ask the office.
duration: Throughout the school year, 2 meetings a month.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High schoolers ages 14 to 18 who live in Brooklyn. BRIC picks students from groups with less access to media training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the class page. Attending every class is required to get the stipend.
notes: The class page says students under 18 need working papers from their school. Finishing the program makes you eligible for other paid BRIC work, per the page. The page says eight sessions but lists nine Tuesdays, and gives Dec 9 in one place and Dec 8 in another, so confirm the last date.
duration: 8 sessions, 16 hours. Fall 2026: Tuesdays Oct 13 to Dec 8, 4 to 6 p.m.
pay_detail: Free class with a $200 stipend if you attend every session.

who_can_apply: NYC high school age teens. You can apply to only one of the two fellowships. The current page does not list exact ages; the 2023-24 page said NYC sophomores, juniors or seniors, or ages 15 to 19.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You cannot edit it after you submit. Then you have a virtual interview. After that you get an offer and steps to start.
notes: Pay is called a stipend on the page. Working papers are not mentioned for the fellowships, but BRIC requires them for its bootcamps for under 18, so ask. BRIC also accepts youth under 21 for its film festival.
duration: 2026-27 school year. Curatorial meets Wednesdays 4 to 6 p.m. Media meets Thursdays 4 to 6 p.m. In person at BRIC.
pay_detail: $17 per hour for 2 hours a week, paid every two weeks, based on attendance.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Beginners are welcome. You must attend every session; if you miss the first day your spot goes to the waitlist.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the class page.
notes: The class page says students under 18 need working papers from their school. Class is at Clarendon Library in Brooklyn, not at BRIC House. The page text says Mondays but its class-times list shows Thursdays (Oct 8 to Nov 26), so confirm the weekday.
duration: 8 sessions, 16 hours. Fall 2026: Mondays Oct 5 to Nov 30, 4 to 6 p.m. (no class Oct 12). Exhibition Thu, Dec 10, 5 to 7 p.m.
pay_detail: Free class with a $200 stipend if you attend every session.

who_can_apply: All ages can join. Teens under 16 must be with a parent or guardian the whole time, so teens 16 and up can volunteer on their own. Event volunteer roles are usually 18 and up.
how_to_apply: Make a Volunteer Profile with the Volgistics link on the park's volunteer page. Then pick events.
notes: Coastal Cleanup is best suited for ages 10 and up. Tasks happen outdoors on uneven ground. Ask staff about accommodations.
duration: Green Team: twice a month on Saturdays, 10 a.m. to noon, April to October. Coastal Cleanups: about 2 hours each, now and then from April to October. Sign up for as many as you like.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.

who_can_apply: Rising 10th, 11th and 12th graders who live in Brooklyn or go to school in Brooklyn. A strong interest in Brooklyn's past.
how_to_apply: The page does not give steps. It says the 2026 application is closed. Questions: CBHEducation@bklynlibrary.org.
notes: Confirm first: pay, exact dates and application steps are not on the page. The page showed the 2026 application as closed. Ask CBH Education whether it is paid.
duration: Summer. The 2026 program had a final reception; exact weeks and hours are not stated.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page. Ask CBH Education whether there is a stipend.

who_can_apply: Youth from across New York City. Most classes are ages 14 to 19; the Advanced Portfolio class is ages 16 to 24. You do not need to be an artist.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the Studio Programs page. Questions: Phoebe@groundswell.nyc or Brandon@groundswell.nyc (shown on the page), or call 718-254-9782.
notes: The page described the 2025-26 school year, so check the page for the 2026-27 session. Classes are at the Gowanus studio, in person.
duration: The 2025-26 session ran Oct 27 to Mar 12, with one class a week (afternoons, about 2 to 2.5 hours).
pay_detail: Free. No pay is mentioned for the studio classes.

who_can_apply: Youth. Ages, grades and how to join are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Contact Groundswell: Office@groundswell.nyc or 718-254-9782 (shown on the site), or check the Youth section for application news.
notes: Confirm first. The page does not list ages, pay amount or how to apply. It says murals are made throughout New York City, and one project title mentions Queensbridge House.
duration: July to August
pay_detail: The page says youth get stipends and calls it a summer jobs program. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students in 11th or 12th grade, and college students, who like health careers. You must also be processed as a hospital volunteer. That means a form, a medical packet, an in-person interview and a 3-hour orientation.
how_to_apply: Send the intern application and the under-18 release form. Add a short essay (500 words max) on why you want it. Add proof of vaccination (COVID and flu) and two short recommendation letters. Then you have a 15 to 20 minute virtual interview. Questions: Volunteer@maimo.org or 718-283-3980.
notes: Unpaid, so no work permit. Students under 18 may only volunteer 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday to Friday, per the page. Check the page for the year of each deadline.
duration: Three rotation blocks a year: Dec 11 to Mar 10, Mar 11 to May 31, and Jun 1 to Sep 2.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You get a certificate of completion from the hospital.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page says volunteers range in age from 14 to 90 but does not state a minimum teen age. All volunteers need medical clearance, references, an interview, a background check and orientation.
how_to_apply: Download the High School Student Application Packet from the volunteer page. Email it to Volunteer@maimo.org. Or mail it to Department of Volunteer and Student Services, 5014 Fort Hamilton Parkway, Brooklyn, NY 11219. Phone 718-283-3980. They send medical clearance forms after they get your application.
notes: Students under 18 may not volunteer outside 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday. The page says volunteering does not lead to a paid job at Maimonides. Some programs (Feeders, Summer Youth) go through partner schools.
duration: At least two 4-hour shifts a week. In the school year, volunteers under 18 must give at least 6 hours per workweek.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get a cafeteria meal voucher and discounted parking. A recommendation letter is offered after at least 150 hours.

who_can_apply: High school students entering their senior year. Strong essay needed. You must be free Monday to Friday for all four weeks with no vacation or summer classes.
how_to_apply: Email the form and an essay as one PDF to Volunteer@maimo.org. Put "Science Scholars" and the year in the subject line. Add a parent waiver form. If accepted, you also finish the hospital volunteer form, the medical packet and an in-person interview by May 20.
notes: Formerly named Women in Science. Led by the Chief of Colon and Rectal Surgery. Incomplete applications are not looked at. Accepted students also go through the hospital volunteer process. Ask whether it is paid.
duration: 4 weeks. The 2026 session ran Mon, July 6 to Fri, July 31, 2026.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students who will be between 15.5 and 18 years old. U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or international students with a valid F-1 visa. All experience levels are welcome.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Pratt PreCollege form. It opens in November. Students are billed in mid-April and payment is due right away. Scholarship forms are separate. Email: precollege@pratt.edu (listed on the page).
notes: Scholarships go to students with strong art work and big money need. The FAQ says winners usually come from homes with income of $60,000 or less. Pratt also has shorter options. They include an Explore program, an online summer program, Saturday classes and one-day workshops.
duration: 4 weeks, 4 college credits. 2027 dates: check-in Tue, July 6; classes July 8 to July 30; exhibition and move out Sat, July 31.
pay_detail: Costs money. The tuition amount was not on the program pages. Budget $300 to $500 more for art supplies, plus metro fare. Need-based scholarships cover tuition, program fees, housing and meal plan.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 for the Teen Service Series. The Park Pitch In weekends are open to teens 14 and up, adults and groups. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Register online for each event through the Alliance volunteer page. Registration is required. Questions: (718) 965-8951. The phone number is listed under Contact Us.
notes: Unpaid volunteering, so no work permit. Some events have age limits, so check the age on each event. The Junior Volunteer Corps is for youth groups with children ages 4 to 13.
duration: Single days. Teen Service Series runs select Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, June to October (times vary). Park Pitch In runs select weekends April to November.
pay_detail: Unpaid and free. You earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Girls and nonbinary students in grades 9 to 12 (rising seniors OK) who live in the New York tri-state area and can commute to campus. Current 8th graders should apply the next year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form on the Bossgirls page. The page strongly discourages submissions generated by AI tools. Check the page for the 2027 opening.
notes: Hours in 2026: 10am to 3pm in weeks 1 and 5, 10am to 1pm in weeks 2 to 4. A search summary said the 2026 deadline was in late February; the page itself gives no date, so confirm.
duration: 5 weeks, Monday to Thursday (2026: June 29 to July 30)
pay_detail: Free (sponsored by Standard Chartered Bank). No pay; it is an enrichment program, not an internship.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page says ages 13 to 18 in one place and 13 to 17 in another, so ask which applies to you. A parent or guardian must sign a consent form.
how_to_apply: Register in advance when a sign-up link appears on the page. Space is limited. You get an email the Thursday before with details and a waiver. Use the contact link on the page for questions.
notes: No one can join without the waiver. Check the page often, because sessions fill up.
duration: Saturdays 1:00 to 2:00 pm, April to June and September to December
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 or freshman year of college. The commuter option is for students who live in or near NYC. Academic strength is what the admissions team looks for.
how_to_apply: Online application. Columbia says applications are reviewed on the dates-and-deadlines schedule; early registration is cheaper to plan around.
notes: Expensive; the page says financial aid details are elsewhere and they were not read. The commuter page still shows a $95 application fee under a Summer 2026 cost heading while the cost page for Summer 2027 says $80. Free Columbia programs for NYC teens (Double Discovery Center, Freedom and Citizenship) exist but their pages blocked access, so they are not listed.
