duration: 1 week (Jun 21 to 25, 2027) or 3 weeks (Jun 28 to Jul 16, 2027; more sessions listed on the dates page).
pay_detail: 1-week session $2,883. 3-week session $6,381. Plus an $95 application fee and $50 or more for course materials. Deposit $1,000 (1-week) or $2,000 (3-week) is credited toward the cost. These are estimates pending trustee approval.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors based in the New York City area. You must come to every weekly meeting at the museum.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Smithsonian application system (SOLAA). The application has short answer questions, an essay and two references. The references are adults who are not related to you. A teacher or mentor works. You can save and finish later. A virtual info session was offered. See the page.
notes: Meets at 2 East 91st Street and some offsite places. The page says the demographic and citizenship questions are optional and not tied to your application. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed. Cooper Hewitt also runs free monthly Teen Drop-In workshops and a Design Career Fair.
duration: Tuesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM, Jan 19 to Jun 1, 2027, with NYC school breaks off
pay_detail: $1,250 stipend after you finish the program.

who_can_apply: New York City public or charter high school students in grades 9 to 12. The page says students meet a mix of these: attend a school without a full visual arts program, qualify for free school meals, or come from a low or moderate income household. No art experience needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online registration form on the Saturday Program page when it is open. No recommendation letter is needed. You get an email when you are accepted. Sign up for the mailing list on the page for the next opening. Office phone and email are on the FAQ page.
notes: Classes are at the Foundation Building, 7 E 7th Street, and 41 Cooper Square. The FAQ page still shows the 2024-2025 year in places, so trust the main page for current dates. There is a year-end show for families.
duration: Saturdays 10 AM to 5 PM through the school year, in a fall and a spring semester
pay_detail: Free to students. The FAQ says round-trip MetroCards are handed out each Saturday on request. This is a class, not a job.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. You are a rising sophomore to rising senior or the same level.
how_to_apply: Fill out the registration form and pay tuition to enroll. The page also links a scholarship section for the Jeffery and Paul Gural Merit Scholarship for NYC Public School Students. Questions: the program email is on the page.
notes: This is a commuter program on campus. The page does not give housing or college credit. The page lists the 2026 year; check the mailing list for the 2027 price.
duration: Four weeks, Monday to Thursday 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM. The 2026 program ran July 13 to Aug 6, 2026. No housing, meals or college credit.
pay_detail: 2026 tuition was $4,350 to $4,500 depending on the course, including a $270 non-refundable registration fee, art materials and field trips. The Gural Merit Scholarship for NYC Public School Students covers full tuition.

who_can_apply: Current high school students who have finished 9th, 10th or 11th grade. Rising 9th graders are not eligible. Open to students from anywhere, but New York City students get priority for financial aid. Some courses need strong math or chemistry grades.
how_to_apply: Apply online when applications open on Dec 11, 2026. See the FAQs on the Summer STEM page for the aid process. The program is selective.
notes: Classes are in person at 41 Cooper Square. The page lists 2026 prices: $3,150 for a 3-week course and $5,150 for a 6-week course. Check the 2027 numbers when applications open.
duration: 3 or 6 weeks, Monday to Thursday 9 AM to 3 PM. The 2026 program ran July 6 to Aug 13, 2026.
pay_detail: 2026 cost was $3,150 per course. Financial aid is available to those who qualify. No housing is provided.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 19 who completed 10th grade by the program start, live in the NYC area (or arrange a supervising adult and housing), and are U.S. citizens or permanent residents at U.S. curriculum schools. No interview or minimum GPA.
how_to_apply: Online application with transcript, two recommendation letters and short essays (250 to 300 words each). Contact: summer@tech.cornell.edu.
notes: Cost is not stated on the page, so confirm the price and any financial aid with the program before applying. Selective. International students are not admitted at this time.
duration: 3 weeks, commuter only (no housing). Exact 2027 dates are not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page (students earn 2 Cornell credits). Ask summer@tech.cornell.edu before applying.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 16 to 24. This includes teens who are pregnant or have kids. You do not need an appointment or a referral.
how_to_apply: Go to 460 West 41 Street, New York, NY any time, or call 212-613-0300. Intake is open 24 hours a day.
notes: This is a support program for teens who are on their own, not a typical job. The details of CovWorks (length, pay, who qualifies) are not on the program pages, so ask staff. If you are in danger right now, call 911.
pay_detail: Free. The site says there is no cost to stay or use the services. Pay for CovWorks training is not stated.

who_can_apply: NYC residents ages 16 to 24 who are not in school and not working. You need at least a 5th grade reading level. You must be authorized to work in the United States. The Advanced Training track needs a high school diploma or HSE.
how_to_apply: The page has no application form. Call DYCD Community Connect at 1-800-246-4646 to find a provider near you.
notes: The page lists these training areas: Healthcare, Construction, Transportation and Culinary Arts. It also lists Digital Marketing. Direct Service Professionals is listed too. The page does not mention a work permit. It does say you must be allowed to work in the United States.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: The page says participants are paid at each program level. It does not state the pay rate.

who_can_apply: 2025 FAQ: rising high school seniors or college students ages 16 to 24 who can legally work in the U.S. and have some prior paid or volunteer work experience.
how_to_apply: Fill out the SYEP application online at application.nycsyep.com and choose a Ladders community partner. Selection uses a personal statement, transcript and resume, then workshops, mock interviews and employer interviews (2025 FAQ).
notes: Competitive. Eligibility, pay and process come from the 2025 FAQ because no newer FAQ was found, so check the DYCD page when applications reopen. Interns under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor). Free to apply.
duration: 6 weeks, 25 to 40 hours a week (2025 FAQ)
pay_detail: At least $16.50 per hour in 2025 (2025 FAQ). 2026 pay is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: NYC high school juniors and seniors who live in New York City, are low income (or meet an exception such as public assistance, foster care or living in a high-poverty area) and meet at least one other listed need. The page lists age 16 to 21 in one place and 14 to 21 in another, so ask a provider.
how_to_apply: Contact a Learn & Earn provider from the DYCD list, or call DYCD Community Connect at 1-800-246-4646. Providers check your eligibility.
notes: Income-based, with extra eligibility rules listed on the page. Teens under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Year-round program with a six-week paid summer internship
pay_detail: Paid six-week summer internship. Rate not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Drop-in centers are for youth up to age 24 and their families. Housing for independent living is for ages 16 to 24 who have no home. The page does not state ages for crisis shelter and outreach.
how_to_apply: Use the discoverDYCD site to find a drop-in center, shelter or housing site near you. The page does not give a phone number.
notes: This is a safety and housing service, not a job. If you are in danger right now, call 911. The Door and Covenant House (other cards) also take walk-ins.
pay_detail: The page does not list a cost.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who live in the five boroughs of NYC and are legally allowed to work in the U.S. Some options (school-based, NYCHA, foster care, homeless youth) have extra rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online at application.nycsyep.com or on paper with an SYEP provider. One application only. Community-based placements are picked by random lottery. Have ID documents ready (proof of age, identity, address, Social Security).
notes: Pay and hours above are the 2026 numbers and may change. Free to apply. NYS Department of Labor says anyone 14-17 needs working papers (employment certificate) to hold a job in New York State; ask your SYEP provider what they need from you. Teens in school-based (CareerReady) options apply through their school. You pay your own transportation and meals.
duration: 6 weeks
pay_detail: Ages 16-24 (2026): $17.00 per hour, 25 hours a week. Ages 14-15 (2026): up to $700 for about 12.5 hours a week.

who_can_apply: NYC residents ages 16 to 24 who are not in school and not working. The page also lists a high school diploma or equivalent. It also lists U.S. work authorization. Males must register with Selective Service.
how_to_apply: The page has no application form. Call DYCD Community Connect at 1-800-246-4646 to find a provider near you.
notes: The page says the program is for ages 16 to 24 who are not in school and not working. Target industries are Infrastructure, Healthcare, Technology, Media and Government. The page does not state the pay rate, the program length or whether a work permit is needed.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: The page says the program includes paid internships. It does not state the pay rate.

who_can_apply: NYC residents legally allowed to work in the U.S. who took part in the 2026 Summer Youth Employment Program as CareerReady (ages 16 to 19 in a CareerReady partner high school) or in Special Initiatives (ages 16 to 20, in high school or a high school equivalency program), as of Oct 26, 2026.
how_to_apply: Use the WLG online application (CareerReady or Special Initiatives link), or ask your SYEP provider for help. If selected, submit documents online or in person to your provider.
notes: Only for teens who were in 2026 SYEP through a partner school or Special Initiatives provider, so most teens cannot start here. Internet access is required. The application deadline has passed. Teens under 18 need NYS working papers (NYS Department of Labor).
duration: 22-week program. The page does not state start or end dates.
pay_detail: New York State minimum wage, paid every two weeks (DYCD FAQ).

who_can_apply: Youth in foster care and youth who have left foster care in New York City, from 6th grade through age 26.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Sign-up for Coaching form on the ACS Fair Futures page, or call 212-676-8609. Your foster care agency may also help.
notes: Also open to younger kids. Support, not a paid job. Ask your coach about paid internships.
pay_detail: Not a job. A cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors attending a New York City high school. Not every accepted student is matched with a site.
how_to_apply: Online application with short-answer questions and a resume, then an interview with the Futures and Options team. Then they try to match you to a site. Use the interest form on the page to get a notice when it opens. Questions: programquestions@futuresandoptions.org.
notes: Pay rate, season and length are not on the page, so confirm first. Futures and Options is based in Manhattan but serves NYC students from every borough. It also runs Career Essentials workshops (the fall application closed Oct 7, 2026).
duration: Not stated. Internship hours plus two orientations and a series of workshops.
pay_detail: The page says the internships are paid. The pay rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: New York City students who are about to graduate from high school. You like business, finance, government or public policy.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the page. You will be told when the application opens.
notes: The page says 930 students have been ULF interns since 1996 and alumni have received $1.7 million in scholarships. Rate and dates are not stated.
duration: 6 weeks in the summer
pay_detail: Paid summer internship. The hourly rate is not stated. At the end you get a book and technology stipend and can apply for college scholarships.

who_can_apply: Driven high school juniors who are on track to graduate and allowed to work in the U.S. You can have a lighter class load in senior year for the internship. Students at partner schools apply in the fall or winter of junior year.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the Genesys Works site and pick New York. If accepted you get an email to interview for a spot in summer training. You provide your own transportation to training and to the internship.
notes: The page says Genesys Works works with set schools, so ask your counselor if your school is a partner. The direct New York link on the location page gave a not-found error. Use the main Apply Now button or email info.nyc@genesysworks.org. Many schools give credit for the training and internship.
duration: 8 weeks of summer training (160 hours) between junior and senior year, then a year-long internship of about 20 hours a week during the school year
pay_detail: Hourly rates vary by site. The page says interns can make about $10,000 to $12,000 over the internship year. Another spot on the site says $10,000 to $13,000.

who_can_apply: Students going into grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Send the application form. Add one letter from a teacher, coach, counselor, boss or camp counselor. A committee reads them. Only some applicants get an interview. Call 212-423-3254 with questions.
notes: Because there is a stipend, ask the museum about working papers for under 18. The page does not say. Check the museum site for the next call.
duration: Spring training, then the 2026 to 27 school year
pay_detail: Interns get a stipend. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: U.S. citizens or permanent residents who come from a low-income household and/or are first-generation college students (neither parent has a bachelor's degree). The program checks income with tax papers such as a 1040. Grade levels and school lists are not stated on the pages.
how_to_apply: Ask the program for the forms by email. You need the application and the recommendation forms. The Eligibility and Selection page lists who to write to: the Program Director or the Curriculum Coordinator. The form asks about you and your money. It also asks for a personal statement.
notes: This is a federal TRIO program that gets funding from the U.S. Department of Education. The pages do not say how many students are accepted or which schools it serves. Ask the program before you plan around the summer dates.
duration: School-year activities plus a four-week summer academic program with high school level classes at John Jay, living on a college campus
pay_detail: Free to the student. The page says all Upward Bound activities and services are free. A stipend is not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in 10th or 11th grade. Not residential.
how_to_apply: Step 1: fill out the Program Registration Form. Step 2: pay with the Program Payment Form. Both steps are needed to confirm a spot. The contact is listed on the page.
notes: The page says to register early because the program has hit its limit in past years. Confirm that registration is open before you plan around it. The prices on the page are the 2026 prices.
duration: 4 days, July 19 to 22, 2027, 9 AM to 3 PM each day
pay_detail: $500 if you register before June 1 and $550 before July 1 (the page shows 2026 prices). The fee includes a light breakfast each day and a T-shirt. Finishers get a certificate and a $75 application fee waiver for the chemical engineering degree.

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in 10th or 11th grade. Not residential.
how_to_apply: Step 1: fill out the Program Registration Form. Step 2: pay with the Program Payment Form. Both are needed to confirm participation. The contact is listed on the page.
notes: Confirm that registration is open before you plan around it. Page pricing is $500 before May 1 and $550 before June 1, which does not match pay_detail; pay_detail needs a human check. The page also lists a free Summer Engineering Awareness Program. It lasts six or ten days.
duration: 4 days, July 19 to 22, 2027
pay_detail: $400 before May 1 and $450 before June 1.

who_can_apply: Any high school student.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Institute Registration Form to pick your weeks, then pay for each week with the Program Payment Form. Both steps are required to hold a spot.
notes: Contact details are on the page. The registration and payment forms are separate, and both are needed. The form link uses the old Manhattan College name. The form page did not load as text, so confirm it is open before you plan around it.
duration: Six one-week sessions from July 5 to Aug 12, 2027, Monday to Thursday 9 AM to 2:30 PM. You can attend one or more weeks. Not residential.
pay_detail: $600 per week. Finishing at least one week earns a certificate and a no-cost application to the engineering program (a $75 value).

who_can_apply: Motivated high school students. The page lists students going into 10th, 11th or 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Use the pre-college sign-up form linked on the O'Malley page when it reopens.
notes: Manhattan University is in Riverdale in the Bronx. Check the page for 2027 prices and dates.
duration: 2026 session: June 22 to July 31, 2026, with a one-week in-person intensive July 13-17, 2026 plus five weeks online
pay_detail: 2026 cost: $6,000 tuition. A residential option adds $1,000 per week for room and board ($7,000 total).

who_can_apply: Students currently enrolled in 10th or 11th grade who are entering their junior or senior year. You must stay in the residence.
how_to_apply: The page lists the School of Engineering contact for details. The phone is 718-862-7281. The email is deanengr@manhattan.edu. No sign-up form is linked for this program.
notes: Parents can come to the closing ceremony and final project contest. Other short summer engineering programs on the same page cost less or are free.
duration: 7 days, Aug 1 to 7, 2027, living on campus
pay_detail: $2,500 total, which covers tuition, room and board, supplies and events.

who_can_apply: Students now enrolled in 10th or 11th grade. The page says selection is based in part on strong math and science skills and interest in engineering.
how_to_apply: The page gives no application form. It says to complete the registration form, and the page lists the program director, Dr. Walter P. Saukin, at 718-862-7171 (Monday to Friday, 9:30 AM to 4 PM). Call to ask how to apply.
notes: The school is now called Manhattan University, formerly Manhattan College. The page says the program has run for over 40 years. The page lists a free program. It comes with a certificate and no fee to apply at Manhattan University. The page lists an email for the director that does not match the director's name, so call instead. Confirm the steps with the director.
duration: Choose a 6-day or 10-day session. The page lists 2027 dates: June 25-26 and June 28 to July 1 (8 AM to 3 PM); July 7-9, 12-16 and 19-20 (10-day program, 8:30 AM to 3 PM); and July 22-23 and 26-29.
pay_detail: Free to participants. Corporate and individual sponsors pay for it. You get a certificate and an application fee waiver at Manhattan University.

who_can_apply: Students 16 and older. Some roles, such as Maternal Child Health, require 18. Montefiore also partners with SYEP. Its SYEP provider is Children's Arts and Sciences Workshop.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Summer Volunteer - High School posting on Montefiore's career site (linked from the volunteer page), then attend an orientation and interview. Interviews are first come, first served.
notes: Confirm first: the dates are from the 2025 posting. Contact: volunteerservices@montefiore.org (shown on the page).
duration: Summer session runs June to September; minimum 100 hours; each session at least 3 to 4 hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 15 or older. JuMP is for ages 15 to 17 and requires full availability for all six weeks. Unit Support is open to high school students. The emergency department and some other roles are 18+.
how_to_apply: Online application, one letter of recommendation from a non-relative, and a resume.
notes: Read through the fetch tool because direct downloads were blocked. The page says volunteers need a valid Social Security number (a hospital clearance rule on the official site) and pay for their own medical clearance. Other Mount Sinai campuses have their own pages and age rules that were not read.
duration: JuMP: 6 weeks, 100 hours. Unit Support: one 3-hour shift a week; the page lists a 100 hour minimum for high school students.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page lists no JuMP cost or pay.

who_can_apply: High school students interested in health care who can attend the full month. The page wants motivated, mature students with volunteer experience. Ten students are accepted.
how_to_apply: Watch the Lenox Hill volunteer page for the next call for forms. If you have a question, write to the Manhattan campus volunteer team. The email is manhattancampusvolunteers@northwell.edu.
notes: The page is out of date, so check with the volunteer team to see if there is a 2027 program. The regular junior volunteer program has different rules and needs working papers.
duration: At least 100 hours in July, at least four days a week (Monday to Thursday) from 9 AM to 3 PM. No vacation during that time.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. No cost is listed.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16 at the Manhattan hospitals. Junior volunteers (ages 16 to 17) hand in working papers and a parent consent form. All applicants are interviewed, then there is a six-month trial period.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the Lenox Hill volunteer page. There is an interview. There is a required orientation. You also need a medical clearance. Questions? Write to manhattancampusvolunteers@northwell.edu.
notes: The page says junior volunteers (ages 16 to 17) must submit working papers and a parental consent form. Orientation and medical clearance are required. Volunteers 18 and older must pass a background screening. The page asks for 100 hours a year. The page gives a minimum age of 16 and no maximum age.
duration: 100 hours per calendar year is required. Onboarding takes about 6 to 8 weeks.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer. No cost is listed.

who_can_apply: Explainers are high school students. The page does not state a grade or age range. Interns work one weekend shift a week.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application by the deadline. Complete applications get an invite to a group interview at the Children's Adventure Garden. Accepted teens attend orientation with a parent or guardian and 24 hours of training before starting.
notes: Questions: explainers@nybg.org. Intern tier is unpaid, so a work permit is not clearly needed there; the paid tiers are jobs and the page does not say what papers are required. The orientation date printed on the page shows the wrong year, so confirm it with NYBG. Late applications roll to the next session.
duration: Spring 2027 internship: one 4.5 hour Saturday or Sunday shift each week, Mar 20 to Jun 19, 2027 (the page lists both 105 and 125 service hours; confirm with NYBG), plus 4 required training days (Mar 6, 7, 13, 14, 2027).
pay_detail: Intern tier is unpaid volunteering (OMNY card help for transit can be provided). Later tiers (Advanced Explainer, Mentor, Senior) are paid part-time jobs; the page gives no hourly rate.

who_can_apply: Applicants must be at least 16 (18 for some programs; check each campus). The Queens and Hudson Valley campuses do not offer Summer Only volunteering. Spots are limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application and choose Summer Only plus your preferred program and campus. A volunteer services representative contacts you for an interview if a spot is open.
notes: Many NYP roles (emergency department, palliative care and others) are 18+. Brooklyn Methodist also runs a Junior Volunteer Program that was marked full when searched; its own page was not read for details. This entry covers the system-wide Summer Only option only.
duration: Minimum 120 service hours over the summer.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering.

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old at the start of the program. Under 18 cannot volunteer during the school year. The year-round program is 18 and older.
how_to_apply: Online application, a group information session, full summer availability, onboarding, health clearance (TB test, MMR and varicella proof, flu shot) and a background check.
notes: The Brooklyn campus requires age 18+. Long Island has its own teen program (not read in detail). The FAQ page still shows old 2022 dates, so only the Manhattan page was used for dates. Med-career internships and research are handled separately through HRNTV@NYULangone.org. The Manhattan page and the volunteer page do not mention working papers, so the work permit answer is unknown.
duration: 8 weeks, two 6-hour shifts a week (100 service hours total).
pay_detail: Unpaid. The FAQ says no pay or school credit is given.

who_can_apply: Students who have completed grade 9, 10 or 11 by the program start. No age rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Online application, a 250 to 500 word essay about why you want the course, and an official high school transcript. Contact 212-998-7006 or sps.hsacademy@nyu.edu.
notes: Costs money and gives no college credit or certificate (students get an NYU transcript with a grade). Page does not say whether class is in person.
duration: One week per course (2026 had six weekly sessions, June 29 to Aug 7)
pay_detail: $2,579 tuition per course, $50 application fee, optional housing and dining $684 (summer 2026 prices). No financial aid or discounts offered.

who_can_apply: Full-time NYC residents who attend NYC schools, applying as 10th or 11th graders (rising juniors and seniors), with strong grades and interest in STEM. Students from groups underrepresented in STEM are encouraged to apply.
how_to_apply: Online application (optional recommendation due after), a group interview and lab tours to pick your placement.
notes: Selective with limited spaces. Funded by the Pinkerton Foundation. Students present at an AMNH poster symposium at the end. The two NYU pages differ slightly on grade wording (10th or 11th grade now versus rising juniors and seniors), which is the same group. The program name on a second page reads Applied Research In Science and Engineering. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 10 weeks: about 4 weeks of remote after-school workshops in June, then 6 weeks of in-person lab work (about 150 hours of lab experience). Summer 2026 ran Jun 1 to Aug 14, 2026.
pay_detail: Free. A $2,000 stipend is paid for completing the program.

who_can_apply: Students in 10th grade at a New York City high school. You show strong effort in school. Most Fellows apply with a GPA of 87 or above. You come from an under-resourced community. Your household income (AGI) is under $125,000. You should not already have similar college and career help. You must commit to the whole program.
how_to_apply: Sign the interest form on the Apply page to get an email when the application opens. The online application takes a couple of hours. It needs your transcript, family facts and two recommendation forms. One is from a teacher. One is from a counselor or advisor. Chosen applicants are invited to group interviews. The page puts these in late March.
notes: Admitted Fellows must come to all days of the Summer Institute. A family member must come to an orientation. The application asks for household income. The program uses it to check the income limit. The pages do not say if a work permit is needed.
duration: Six years. Starts with the OppNet Summer Institute (length not stated on the page), then weekly after-school workshops in 11th and 12th grade.
pay_detail: Fellows do paid summer internships or enrichment programs (five summers over the six years). The page does not state the pay.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older by the first day of work. The test page said 16 by July 18, 2026. You must swim 50 yards and meet the vision rule.
how_to_apply: Register for a qualifying test on the Parks page when dates open (or join the notice list). Pass the swim and vision test, then do the training. A letter from an eye doctor can replace the on-site vision exam.
notes: The two Parks pages disagree on the swim time. The main page says 50 yards in 50 seconds or less. The test page says 50 yards in 40 seconds or less with proper form. Plan for the faster one. The pages do not say whether a work permit is needed for 16 and 17 year olds.
duration: Training course of 16 sessions, then the summer season. Beaches open Memorial Day weekend and outdoor pools open in late June. Both close the Sunday after Labor Day. You work five or six days a week.
pay_detail: $22 per hour for lifeguards who finish training and get a post. Lifeguards also get a $908 training payment after the summer season.

who_can_apply: Students entering high school in New York City. The program starts with career exploration in 9th grade, and college courses can begin as early as 10th grade. The page does not list entry rules for each school.
how_to_apply: The page says admission is unscreened (Educational Option method). Attend an information session, open house or high school fair, then rank a P-TECH school as a top choice on your high school application. Check each school's process on its website or at MySchools.nyc.
notes: This is a school choice made before 9th grade, so it fits 8th graders and their families. The page names five schools in Manhattan and the Bronx. Examples are Inwood Early College for Health and Information Technologies and Urban Assembly New York Harbor School. Check each listing to see how students get in.
duration: Six years or less (grades 9 to 14)
pay_detail: The degree is free: courses, materials and college textbooks cost nothing. Internships are listed as a possible part of work-based learning; pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students who are seen as leaders at school, often through student government. Members are voted in at the borough meetings. Each year, two student reps are voted onto the Panel for Educational Policy.
how_to_apply: There is no open form on the page. Ask your school counselor or student government adviser how students are chosen for the borough council. Elections for the Chancellor's council happen at the borough meetings.
notes: There are six borough councils: one in each borough, with two in Brooklyn. The page does not list contacts or meeting dates. It is a leadership role, not a job.
duration: Borough councils meet monthly. The Chancellor's council meets monthly from October through June at the central office.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No cost is listed.

who_can_apply: Students at least 14 and now in high school. You can be outdoors for 2 hours. You have your own ride to the site. You pass an interview. You come to 5 of 6 classes.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application on the internship page, then do a virtual interview. Contact: Erica Chow (email on the page).
notes: This is a learning internship, not a job, and it costs $200 unless you get aid. You must find your own transportation. Supported by Con Edison and other funders per the page. The page says 5 of 6 classes in its eligibility section but 6 out of 7 dates for spring and fall, so ask which applies.
duration: 6 sessions of 3 hours per season (9:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.). Spring 2027: Saturdays Mar 27 to May 8. Summer 2027: Tuesdays or Wednesdays, July 6 to Aug 11. Fall 2027: Saturdays Sept 18 to Oct 23.
pay_detail: $200 fee after you are accepted. Financial aid is available on request and needs no paperwork.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 17. You must attend an interview and an orientation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Volunteer form on the volunteer page. Return it to the volunteer coordinator before the deadline. Then you have an interview and an orientation.
notes: The page lists deadline months, not the year. Popular program, so apply early.
duration: One of three semesters. Fall and spring: one day a week after school. Summer: up to 3 days a week for 6 weeks in July and August, plus a late June orientation.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says you can earn school credit or work experience.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students ages 12 to 18. Only the student should fill out the application, not a parent.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the form on the page. Applications only, no walk-ins.
notes: Popular program with an acceptance step and a waitlist. Mostly outdoors, weather permitting. The museum is the Queens County Farm Museum.
duration: 9 months of select Sundays, 1 to 3 p.m. 2026-27 dates: Oct 11 through June 6, 2027. Certification ceremony June 20.
pay_detail: Unpaid and free. No admission fee. You earn a certificate if you attend at least 13 of 16 sessions.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 18. Junior volunteers cannot serve on weekends or late evenings.
how_to_apply: Call Volunteer Services at 718-670-5952 to book an in-person interview. No walk-ins. Bring a valid ID (state, school or passport), a working permit and one professional letter of recommendation. Then you need medical clearance (doctor form, urine drug screen, flu shot). You also go to a 4-hour orientation.
notes: The hospital lists a "Working Permit" as a requirement for junior volunteers. This may mean New York working papers. Ask the Volunteer Services office which work permit paper they accept. The page says volunteering does not guarantee a job. Hospital address: 4500 Parsons Blvd, Flushing.
duration: Commit to 125 hours of service. Onboarding usually takes several weeks.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens, with a focus on BIPOC and other under-served Queens youth. The page does not list exact ages, grades or home address rules, so ask the museum.
how_to_apply: Send in the QTI 2026-27 form through the Submittable link on the Queens Museum announcement. Phone 718-592-9700. Email info@queensmuseum.org.
notes: This is the fifth year of the program. Ages, grades and work-permit rules are not stated on the announcement, so ask the museum.
duration: 9 months of weekly hybrid sessions (in person and online). No more than 4 absences. Start and end dates are not stated.
pay_detail: $1,000 stipend for the 9-month commitment, plus extra money for travel. QTI teens can also be considered for other paid Queens Museum jobs like workshop assistant and camp counselor.

who_can_apply: New York City residents who are currently in high school or college in New York City. You do not need to love science. NYSCI wants curious students who will try new things and practice public speaking.
how_to_apply: Online application form (linked from the page). You can also fill out an interest form to get a reminder and an invite to an info session. Questions: ebautista@nysci.org (listed on the page).
notes: NYSCI is at 47-01 111th St., Corona, Queens. The youth page lists "Young Adults, Age 14-24" in the site menu; the Explainer page itself does not state a minimum age, so confirm. The apply form link on the page showed as closed when read. Pay rate not stated. Work permit not stated on the page.
duration: One full year, including the summer. High school students work at least 5 hours a week (weekends). You must attend every day of orientation first.
pay_detail: The page calls it an education and youth employment program and says you "work" at NYSCI. The hourly rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors with a cumulative average of 92 (no test scores needed), or an average of 90 plus an SAT of 1210 or an ACT of 25. An interview may be required.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application with a parent consent form and an unofficial transcript. A counselor recommendation form and the official transcript come next. Contact: 718-990-7533. The number is on the page.
notes: Costs money and is for strong students. Check the page in spring for 2027 dates and price.
duration: About 5 weeks. In 2026, July 7 to August 10, classes Monday to Thursday for 2 hours.
pay_detail: $1,000 per course, due July 1 (2026 price). Students who later enroll at St. John's get a $2,000 High School Scholars Grant, renewable for up to four years.

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors or seniors who are at least 16 when the program starts. Students from outside NYC and outside the Tri-State area may apply but get no help with housing or travel. No GPA minimum. Sophomores are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Apply online. You also need a letter of recommendation and a transcript (to show you are in high school). Selected applicants get a Zoom interview.
notes: Very competitive (about 32 students a year). You must attend the entire program with no gaps. Minors cannot work with human patients. You may not use SSRP work in science competitions. Contact: program administrator listed on the page, 1230 York Ave.
duration: 7 weeks, Mon Jun 21 to Thu Aug 5, 2027, full time (about 35 hours a week, roughly 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
pay_detail: Free to apply and attend. An OMNY card covers NYC transit. Stipends are not guaranteed; need-based stipends may go to students with financial hardship who meet all attendance rules.

who_can_apply: Young women and gender-expansive youth in 10th or 11th grade who live in New York City or Newark and can come in person once a week. No academic rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the link on the Leadership Scholars page. Questions: Charlie Ambrose, charlie@sadienash.org (listed on the page).
notes: The page lists the New York City office at 247 W 37th Street, Suite 705, New York, NY 10018. Stipend is based on participation.
duration: Thursdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., November to May, in person at the New York City or Newark office.
pay_detail: Up to $400 at the end of the semester, based on participation.

who_can_apply: High school seniors who are women or gender-expansive youth of color and live in New York City or Newark. No academic rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the link on the Nash U page. Questions: Charlie Ambrose, charlie@sadienash.org (listed on the page).
notes: The apply page says you must identify as a woman or gender-expansive person of color. You must commit for the full internship.
duration: Saturdays 10 a.m. to 12 noon, November 2026 to May 2027, plus some events.
pay_detail: Eligible for a $400 stipend at the end of the internship.

who_can_apply: Young women and gender-expansive youth in grades 9 to 12 who live in New York City or Newark. You commit for the whole program. No academic rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the link on the Siblinghood Academy page. For questions, write to Cielito Pareja at cielito@sadienash.org. The page lists this contact.
notes: No more than 5 absences for the in-person version.
duration: In person: once a week, Tuesdays or Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 p.m., November to May. Virtual: 10 weeks, offered each fall and spring.
pay_detail: In-person: up to $400 at the end. Virtual: up to $150 (you must attend 9 of 10 sessions). Referral bonus of $25 per friend.

who_can_apply: Young women and gender-expansive youth enrolled in high school who live in New York City or Newark and have not done Summer Institute before. No grade or skill rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Apply Now page when the cycle opens, then join a group interview. Sign up for the opportunities email list to hear when it opens. Questions: nashers@sadienash.org.
notes: For young women and gender-expansive youth. The Brooklyn, Queens and other borough sites are part of the same program.
duration: 6 weeks. In 2026: July 6 to Aug 13, Monday to Thursday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., at sites in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Newark.
pay_detail: Eligible for a $450 stipend at the end of the summer, based on participation.

who_can_apply: New York City high school students ages 14 to 18 in grades 9 to 12. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the Apprenticeships page when it opens each March.
notes: Pay is not stated, so ask whether it is paid and whether working papers are needed. The site says the program has run for decades.
duration: July and August, up to 3 days a week, Wednesday to Sunday, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated. The page calls it a service learning experience.

who_can_apply: Staten Island high school students in grades 11 and 12, per the program page.
how_to_apply: Download the application. It is a PDF on the program page. Email the finished form to the program email on the page: Medicalscienceprogram@rumcsi.org.
notes: Session dates, start month and cost are not stated, so call or email to confirm before you plan. The general volunteer page says its openings are filled right now. It states no age rule. The application email could not be read in this check, so confirm it.
duration: Six weeks, one day per week after school.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: High school sophomores, juniors and seniors. No age rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Send the application form, a one-page essay (500 words max) about your goals, and a parent or guardian signature. You can apply online, by mail or by email. Contact: lifelong-learning@wagner.edu, 718-390-3221.
notes: Ask the office whether spring 2027 spots are open and whether the internship is paid.
duration: The fall session runs Oct 2 to Dec 12 (year not stated), on Fridays 5:30 to 8 p.m. or Saturdays 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. (hours depend on class).
pay_detail: No pay or fee is mentioned. You get community service hours and a certificate of completion from Wagner College.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 years old and older who are in high school. Adults over 18 join the regular Docent program.
how_to_apply: Use the Docent application form linked on the zoo volunteer and job page. Candidates must pass the 10-week course. Volunteers go through a background check.
notes: The 2026 class deadline had passed as of 2026-10-09. Check the page around late summer for the next class. Teens learn public speaking and animal presentation skills.
duration: 10-week training course, then ongoing docent shifts.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens who are at least 14 years old. You must be able to work on your own and on a team and be available on a regular basis. Some roles (like animal diet prep) are adults only.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer application form linked on the zoo volunteer page. All volunteers go through a background check. The zoo cannot give status updates. It only contacts qualified candidates.
notes: Limited spaces. Volunteers in animal care jobs must show a negative TB test and proof of COVID-19 vaccination, per the page.
duration: Minimum 3 months, can be extended. Regular availability needed.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: High school-aged youth. No photography experience needed. To get the stipend you must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident or otherwise eligible to work in the U.S., and show valid working papers when accepted.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application (link on the Expanding the Walls page) by Nov 6, 2026. Show valid working papers when you are accepted. Questions: use the contact email on the page.
notes: Meets at 144 W 125th Street. The FAQ on the page still shows the 2026 dates in one spot; the headline dates for 2027 are Jan 9 to Aug 5, 2027. Public school holidays are observed. The page does not state an age range or whether you must live in NYC.
duration: Jan 9 to Aug 5, 2027. Tuesdays 4:00 to 6:30 PM and Saturdays 11 AM to 3 PM, then Tuesday to Thursday 11 AM to 3 PM in the summer.
pay_detail: $1,000 stipend paid at the end of the program, a Canon DSLR camera, and transportation fare to and from the museum. The page says this is not a job or an internship.

who_can_apply: Anyone ages 12 to 24. No documents are needed. Some programs have their own age rules.
how_to_apply: Go to 555 Broome Street, Manhattan, Monday to Friday 2:00 to 5:30 pm (extra hours 10:00 am to 2:00 pm for urgent needs and for youth without stable housing). Or call 212-941-9090 or email membership@door.org.
notes: The Door also has a Bronx drop-in center for runaway and homeless youth. Ask staff for details, because ages for it are not stated. Some job training programs have their own age rules, so ask staff.
pay_detail: Joining is free. Pay is not stated on this page. A separate program, The CUT Culinary Training, lists a stipend (see its card).

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 24. All Door job programs need free Door membership first.
how_to_apply: Become a Door member (free), then contact Latasha Stephens at Lstephens@door.org or 917-696-3758.
notes: Other Door job programs have other age rules, such as 18 to 24 for several of them. Call first to ask about the next start date.
duration: 12 weeks
pay_detail: Stipend of up to $3,100 over 150 hours

who_can_apply: Open to all NYC youth, including current students and recent graduates. No experience needed. The page gives no age range.
how_to_apply: Email youth@transalt.org with questions or use the RSVP link on the Youth Activist Committee page. Meetings are hybrid, and in person is encouraged.
notes: The page describes youth activism and does not mention a work permit. The page lists meetings on the last Friday of each month from 4:30 to 6 PM, and says meetings are hybrid. Confirm before you go.
duration: Monthly meetings. The NYC Public Schools opportunities page lists the last Friday of the month, 4:30 to 6:00 PM (subject to change).
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer activism. No cost is listed.

who_can_apply: New Yorkers ages 14 to 18. The page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Check the NYC Votes Youth Ambassadors page for the next call for applications.
notes: Run by the City of New York Campaign Finance Board. Past ambassadors registered voters at public events and with other city agencies. The pages do not say whether the work is paid or needs a work permit.
duration: Weekly meetings, with weekly summer trips. The full length of the program is not stated.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program pages. Ask the program.

who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 15 years old by July 1 of the program year, eligible to work in the United States. You must be free on weekends and for the full 13 months (June to June). The 2026 page said June 2026 to June 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen. Watch the ACES page for news. If you have questions, write to education@wavehill.org or youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Wave Hill House, where this program meets, is wheelchair accessible. Interns travel off site for some field trips.
duration: 13 months, about 4 to 8 hours each weekend (14 at most), plus two Saturday workshops a month and July weekday training
pay_detail: $17 per hour

who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 16 years old by May 1 of the program year, a New York City resident eligible to work in the United States. The 2026 page asked for May 1, 2026.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen (watch the Forest Project page). Pay runs through SYEP, so you also need a separate SYEP application; for 2026 that was due before March 1. Wave Hill tells interviewed teens which SYEP provider to pick. Questions: youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Fieldwork is hard physical work outdoors with heavy tools on unpaved ground. The Ecology Building has 28 stairs and is not wheelchair accessible. You must be ready to join all of the program.
duration: One summer (exact weeks not stated on the page)
pay_detail: About $2,275 for the summer, paid through the NYC Summer Youth Employment Program (SYEP). You also get credit for one college course.

who_can_apply: Enrolled in high school, 15 years old by July 1 of the program year, a New York City resident eligible to work in the United States. The 2026 page asked for July 1, 2026. You must be free for all 14 months.
how_to_apply: Apply to Wave Hill when applications reopen (watch the WERM page). Questions: youthprograms@wavehill.org.
notes: Courses are taught at Wave Hill and the University of Mount Saint Vincent. Fieldwork is outdoors on rough ground with heavy tools. The Ecology Building is not open to wheelchairs. The page names partners such as the American Museum of Natural History.
duration: 14 months: first summer (July to August), school year (September to June), second summer (July to August)
pay_detail: About $3,500 paid across the whole program, plus credit for three college courses.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 22 at any of the five WCS parks. No borough rule is stated.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form to be told when recruitment opens. Questions go to the park's volunteer email (discoveryguide@wcs.org for the Bronx Zoo).
notes: The apply link is the interest form, not the application. WCS also lists 30+ internships and paid jobs for ages 14 to 24 (WCS Career Lattice) and the Youth JIVE job and volunteer expo in early February. Those pages did not state ages or dates for individual internships, so only this program is listed.
duration: Usually a spring session and a summer session; hours not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteering. WCS says youth volunteers earn over 100 hours of community service.

who_can_apply: NYC high school students. YI Artists: grades 9 to 12. YI Arts Careers: entering grades 10 to 12. YI Introductions: entering grades 10 to 12 who are English Language Learners. YI Leaders: grades 11 to 12 who finished at least one semester of YI Artists or YI Arts Careers.
how_to_apply: Online form for each program (links on the Youth Insights page). YI Leaders is for teens who have already done another Youth Insights program.
notes: The page's closing note also lists YI Introductions graduates as eligible for Leaders. That conflicts with its Open to line. The page lists no program contact. Use whitney.org/contact. The Whitney also runs a separate Open Studio for Teens (free).
duration: YI Artists: one semester after school. Summer programs: length not stated. YI Leaders: yearlong, 3 to 10 hours a week.
pay_detail: YI Leaders is a paid internship; the page does not state the amount.

who_can_apply: NYC public high school students at one of the 130+ schools with CTE programs. Students who finish a state-approved program can earn a CTE endorsement on their diploma.
how_to_apply: Browse programs on NYC MySchools. Talk to your guidance counselor or a Family Welcome Center about admissions and enrollment.
notes: This is a school choice, not a job. Ask your guidance counselor or a Family Welcome Center how enrollment works for your grade. The CTE endorsement needs 44 credits, 5 Regents exams, a technical assessment and work-based learning.
duration: Grades 9 to 12
pay_detail: Part of the school day at no cost. Some work-based learning (such as apprenticeships) can be paid, but pay is not stated on this page.

who_can_apply: Students at participating NYC public high schools. Juniors apply for the apprenticeship.
how_to_apply: Ask your school if it participates. Juniors apply for apprenticeships through the program. The page does not list an application link.
notes: Only at participating schools; the page does not list which ones. Apprentices attend school mornings Monday to Thursday and all day Friday, and work Monday to Thursday afternoons. Apprenticeships are registered with the NYS Department of Labor. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 2 to 3 year apprenticeship starting junior year
pay_detail: Paid work experience. Pay rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Tutors are ages 13 to 18, love working with young kids, have a B or higher in high school math, and bring a laptop.
how_to_apply: Sign up to volunteer on the OneInMath site. Use the register-volunteer page.
notes: The program pages do not list chapter locations. The tutor page's library news mentions North Texas libraries, so ask the group which library near you has a chapter. Re-check 2026-10-10: the tutor page does not say sign-up is ongoing, so status is unconfirmed, not rolling.
duration: 2 to 3 hours a week. Commit to at least one session, preferably a year.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked. Re-check 2026-10-10: the campus page does not say it is enrolling, and the Job Corps student page does not say applications are accepted on an ongoing basis, so status is unconfirmed, not rolling. The campus page footer shows 2023.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: Students from Clifton or Paterson who will be in 10th, 11th or 12th grade in September 2026.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form. Have a recommendation form sent for you. Go to a Teen Summer Program Info Session.
notes: The page gives grades, not ages. 2027 applications open in early spring 2027. You must go to a Teen Summer Program Info Session to apply.
duration: About June 30 to Aug 18, 3 to 4 days a week, 8:30 am to 3 pm
pay_detail: $15.92 per hour (2026), daily lunch, weekly bag of produce, rides between sites

who_can_apply: Any child ages 5 to 18 who lives in Pennsylvania. Ages 8 to 18 (before January 1 of the current year) can join the program and take part in contests. Ages 5 to 7 are Cloverbuds. They do non-competitive activities.
how_to_apply: Look up your county 4-H program. Pick a club. Talk with your county educator. Then sign up in 4-H's ZSuite. If you cannot enroll online, ask the educator for help.
notes: A youth group, not a job. Ask your county educator what clubs and teen leader roles are near you.
duration: Ongoing club membership
pay_detail: Members pay a fee for educational materials. Extra fees vary by county and project area. Financial help is available. Amounts are not stated.

who_can_apply: Be at least 12 and not yet 19. Be a U.S. citizen or a lawful permanent resident (National Headquarters can waive this for some lawfully admitted noncitizens). Attend at least three squadron meetings.
how_to_apply: Find a squadron with the unit locator. Visit a meeting with your parents. Go to at least three weekly meetings. Then fill out the application. You can also ask the squadron about the online application.
notes: No military duty. Cadets can stay in until age 21 and can switch to adult membership at 18. Squadron meetings and costs vary, so ask the squadron near you.
duration: Ongoing. Weekly 2-hour meetings, about one Saturday event a month and a week-long summer encampment (typical, per national page)
pay_detail: Annual dues of $25 to $50 depending on location. Uniform and overnight activity fees are extra. National Headquarters says a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year. Some help is available.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. If your school has no chapter, you can join the Virtual Chapter. It is open if you are homeschooled or in a cyber charter, private or charter school. It is also open if your school has no FBLA chapter. The Virtual Chapter page says members must take a business class. Students at schools with an active FBLA chapter cannot join it.
how_to_apply: Ask your chapter adviser at school. If you do not know who that is, contact Bruce Boncal, PA FBLA Executive Director, bboncal@pafbla.us. Virtual Chapter members fill out an online application signed by a parent.
notes: Virtual Chapter members pay their own travel costs. State office: (570) 398-4652, stateoffice@pafbla.us.
duration: School year; the 2027 State Leadership Conference is April 12 to 14, 2027 at the Hershey Lodge and Giant Center
pay_detail: Yearly dues $18 for high school ($10 national and $8 state). Virtual Chapter dues are $16.

who_can_apply: Students enrolled in agricultural education at a school with an FFA chapter. All students in agricultural education are on the official roster. The page does not state an age rule.
how_to_apply: Sign up for agricultural education at a school that has an FFA chapter. Use the Chapter Locator on the Pennsylvania FFA site to find one near you.
notes: The state page says nearly 16,000 students are members, in four regions. Members compete at chapter, regional, state and national events. The National FFA Organization has its own listing in other cards. This one is the Pennsylvania state page.
duration: Ongoing while you are in agricultural education
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the program pages. Ask your ag teacher.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 in Pennsylvania: public, private, parochial or home schooled. You need an adult sponsor (a teacher, parent or scientist). You must do your own research and your own presentation.
how_to_apply: Pick a research category. Find a sponsor. Use the Find Your Region page for your region's deadlines, forms and location. Turn in any required SRC/IRB approval forms.
notes: A science fair, not a job. Your project may need extra approval forms depending on your research field, so ask your sponsor or Regional Director early. Regional pages list the exact deadlines.
duration: Regional meets January to March; State Meet in May (2026: May 17 to 19)
pay_detail: Costs are not stated on the program pages. Check your region page for fees.

who_can_apply: Boys who live in Pennsylvania, have finished their junior year and have at least one semester of high school left. You cannot have gone to a Boys State before. Leadership, character and school service count.
how_to_apply: Register online on the Keystone Boys State site when registration opens. Posts also sponsor students; use the Legion post locator on the Pennsylvania Legion page.
notes: Boys only. A matching Girls State program is run by the American Legion Auxiliary, not this one. Check the Boys State site for the 2027 location and dates, because 2026 was at Messiah University.
duration: One week (2026 session ran Sunday June 14 to Saturday June 20)
pay_detail: No pay. American Legion posts and the Department pay the fees, so little or no cost to the family.

who_can_apply: Girls in Pennsylvania. The pages do not state grade, citizenship or cost rules, so check the application.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply tab on the Keystone Girls State site (the home page links an application for 2027). The old FAQ says to print and mail the form, then fill out a parent packet before camp. Check with a local Auxiliary unit for sponsorship.
notes: Girls only. The FAQ on the site is still from 2023, so confirm this year's dates, deadline and cost with the program before you plan. The national Auxiliary list shows June 21 to June 26, 2026 while the state site shows 20-25 June 2026.
duration: One week in June
pay_detail: No pay. The page says it is free in most cases; you may pay only for your own travel to Shippensburg University. Bring some cash for snacks and shirts sold during the week.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 at the start of the program. High school students. Crews are based in cities across Pennsylvania.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Student Conservation Association (SCA) website. The state page links to the current openings. It links to the application too. You can email paoutdoorcorps@thesca.org.
notes: Crew locations change by year; check the SCA page for this year's list. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday 7 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. (2026: June 29 to August 7)
pay_detail: $17.31 per hour (2026). Lunch, safety gear and daily transport from a central meeting spot in your city are provided.

who_can_apply: Pennsylvania residents who are in 11th grade when they apply.
how_to_apply: Online application, then a 15-minute Zoom interview. Contact PSEAS@psu.edu or 814-867-0383. The page also lists PGSAS@psu.edu, so confirm the address.
notes: No wage is paid. Page lists a contact email in two spellings, so confirm it.
duration: 2 weeks. Session 1: June 20 to July 2, 2027. Session 2: July 11 to 24, 2027.
pay_detail: No pay. Free for selected students: tuition, room, board, materials and activities are covered.

who_can_apply: Minimum age is 14. The page lists no teen-specific roles; ask which positions accept teens.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked on the page, then email the Volunteer Coordinator at volunteers@ansp.org about specific openings.
notes: The page does not say which areas teens can join. Bird Safe Philly runs April to May and September to November.
duration: Regular time from half a day to several days a week, for at least one year
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students. The page describes Teen Podcast as a program for Philly teens. The page does not list ages or a school-district rule for Teen Sketch.
how_to_apply: Each program has its own Apply now link (a Google form) on the teens page. Questions: teens@philamuseum.org.
notes: The page does not say whether the programs are paid or free, or when the forms close. Email the teen team before you plan around it. The museum also ran A Future of Artists, a June to August 2026 exhibition of work by Philadelphia-area high school students.
duration: Fall 2026 programs. Teen Sketch length is not stated.
pay_detail: Pay or stipend not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17 only.
how_to_apply: Sign up through the Awbury Adventures Summer Camp page. Ask for financial aid BEFORE you sign up, because aid spots are few.
notes: This is training, not a paid job. The page does not say whether graduates get counselor jobs. A 2021 posting on the same site said 2 to 6 trainees were chosen as stipend-paid counselors in training; that is old, so ask.
duration: 2 weeks (June 15 to 26 in 2026)
pay_detail: Summer 2026 price was $675 ($641 for members) for the 2 week session. The camp page says scholarships (75% off) and sliding scale fees (30% to 60% off) are available to families in local zip codes.

who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores, juniors and seniors ages 14 to 18. You must live, go to school or have other ties in Southwest Philadelphia. Priority goes to 49th to 65th Streets between Chester Avenue and the river. You must have a work permit or be able to get one.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application with short written answers. Then you have an in-person interview. If you are hired, you sign up for the city C2L-PHL program. It needs a Social Security card, an ID, proof of citizenship and Philadelphia home address, and a W-9.
notes: Competitive: about 50 students a year across all programs. The page still showed 2025-26 dates when read, so check it for the 2026-27 deadline. The Garden will never ask for birth dates or Social Security numbers by text message.
duration: October to spring in the 2025-26 cycle; some interns continue in summer.
pay_detail: $11 to $12.50 per hour in 2025-26; 8.5 hours a week in the school year. Some interns can continue in summer at 20 hours a week.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors in Philadelphia. The page does not state an age range or residency proof.
how_to_apply: The page gives no intern application steps. Contact info@philaculture.org or 215-557-7811.
notes: Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer. The permit is not mentioned on the page.
duration: Eight weeks, up to 35 hours a week (2026: June 19 to August 14); select interns may continue in a school-year program up to 10 hours a week
pay_detail: $20+ per hour for Summer 2026, plus transportation and meal support

who_can_apply: Philadelphia residents ages 12 to 24. In-school youth get priority. You can apply to one program per cycle.
how_to_apply: Apply through the C2L-PHL Youth Portal (phila.gov/c2l-phl). Documents: photo ID, school records, Social Security card, birth certificate or passport, and a work permit. Not first come, first served. Help: C2LPHL@jevs.org or 833-750-5627.
notes: Application is English only; call for help in other languages. Roughly 8,000 city-funded slots a summer (per PYN's site). Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Summer program (plus school-year programming)
pay_detail: Stipend on a prepaid debit card, paid every other week; total $1,300 to $1,500 depending on the program (hourly rate not listed).

who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Pennsylvania Wing page lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: The squadron page does not describe a visit process. Contact the squadron: cc214@pawg.cap.gov (squadron commander) or 215-531-2278. The wing's Join CAP page has the cadet steps.
notes: The Pennsylvania Wing lists five other squadrons in the Philadelphia area. They are Willow Grove, Liberty, Griffin, Gen Carl A Spaatz and Chester County. Ask the wing which is closest to you. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.
duration: The squadron meets Fridays from 7:00 to 9:15 p.m. at the Naval Support Activity Center, 700 Robbins St, Philadelphia, PA 19111.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors with a biology, chemistry or research background. Admission is competitive.
how_to_apply: Submit transcripts and two letters of recommendation. Contact camp assistant Ipatia Daigle (ied26@drexel.edu) or director Dr. Jed Shumsky (js52@drexel.edu).
notes: Drexel runs other Summer Institutes (arts and sciences, business, engineering, design, nursing, public health); their pages did not list grades, costs or dates when read.
duration: 10 days, in-person commuter (2026: July 20 to 31)

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not list ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Drop in at 719 Catharine St, or email cy@fleisher.org.
notes: Not a job. Lead support from the William Penn Foundation and others is listed on the page.
duration: Tuesdays and Wednesdays, 4 to 6 pm, while Philadelphia schools are in session. Fall 2026 workshops start Sept 8.
pay_detail: Free. No attendance requirement. Snacks and bus passes provided.

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old who finished both high school biology and chemistry. Neither can be taken at the same time. Open to students in the Philadelphia Tri-State area. You can apply to a Philadelphia-only section.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google form application. It cannot be saved, so a PDF version is available to draft offline. Two letters of recommendation are required. One must come from a science or STEM teacher who has known you at least a year. Applications are blind reviewed. Then three committee members interview 20 to 25 applicants.
notes: The FAQ says the application launches in mid to late October, so it may open any day now. Check the page for the real dates. General Fox Chase number: 888-369-2427. A summer fellows track is funded by National Cancer Institute grants. Its pay and rules are not stated on the pages.
duration: 11 weeks of Saturday sessions from early January to mid March: Section 1 meets 8:30 to 11:30 a.m. and Section 2 meets 12:30 to 3:30 p.m. There are 16 seats, 8 per section.
pay_detail: Nearly all programming is cost free to participants. No pay for the winter course. Fox Chase cannot provide transportation.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 8 who live in the Philadelphia area.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply to the PACTS Program online form on the page.
notes: For younger teens (grades 6 to 8). Older teens can join the Franklin Ambassador program through STEM Scholars, which has its own card.
duration: School year, workshops meet twice a month on Saturday mornings
pay_detail: Free program.

who_can_apply: Students living in Philadelphia and surrounding areas who are entering 9th grade, interested in STEM, able to commit to four years, with a 3.0 GPA (per FAQ). Non-freshmen are rarely accepted.
how_to_apply: Online application, essay, transcript, two recommendation letters, then an interview with Youth Programs staff.
notes: The FAQ timing and the 'currently closed' message are not fully consistent, so confirm on the page. The sister middle-school program PACTS is for grades 6 to 8.
duration: Four years, grades 9 to 12; research window of 10 weeks between late June and early September
pay_detail: Free to students; rising seniors are paid for lab research (rate not stated). Fees covered by donors.

who_can_apply: Philadelphia teens about to enter grades 10 to 12 who go to a high school in the city. You must be allowed to work in Philadelphia. If you are under 18, you must be able to get a work permit. You must be free for the whole program. It runs June through August, plus some Saturdays in September.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google form linked from the page. Early applications get interviews first.
notes: Funded by The W.W. Smith Charitable Trust and The Hamilton Family Charitable Trust, both named on the page.
duration: June through August, plus select Saturdays in September
pay_detail: Described as a ten-week paid work and learning experience. The hourly rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: Students 16 or older who can keep a regular weekly shift. Needs two school references from teachers and proof of vaccines (measles, mumps, rubella and a TB test).
how_to_apply: Send the application, two letters of support from teachers and shot forms to the Volunteer Services Department. You can send by mail, scan, fax or email. Phone: 215-612-4170.
notes: Facts come from the 2024 application packet on the Jefferson site. The program web page shows only its title (checked 2026-10-09 with a normal fetch and with curl), so the age, time, pay and how-to-apply details are not confirmed on the page. Confirm the current dates, ages and form first. Spots are limited.
duration: 8 weeks, 4 hours a day, one day a week
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get their own transportation.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: the Philadelphia campus page lists transportation and no dorms. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists transportation to and from campus, breakfast and lunch, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: Students now in high school or college from the greater Philadelphia area, including Camden, NJ. You must be able to prove you can work in the United States. No age or grade is stated. The committee gives strong preference to students from groups underrepresented in science.
how_to_apply: Use the MSAP Applications page on monell.org when it opens. Sign up for Monell's newsletter for updates. Questions: AcademicAffairs@monell.org or 267-519-4700. About 200 applications come in each year. 18 to 24 students are usually enrolled.
notes: Minors do not need working papers to apply. They must get them after they are admitted. They come from the School District of Philadelphia, per the Monell FAQ. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer. Monell does not provide housing or meals. Students must commit to the full program with no vacations.
duration: The program page says eight weeks of paid full-time structured research. The 2026 program ran June 15 to July 31, 2026, which is shorter than eight weeks, so confirm the length. The page does not give the 2027 dates.
pay_detail: Described as paid. The amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 22 at the high school sites. Ages 10 to 13 are served at middle school sites. A parent or guardian must sign and provide extra information before a youth under 18 can be enrolled.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Student Inquiry Form on the Mural Arts enroll page. It is not an application and does not confirm enrollment. An Art Education staff member follows up about classes near you. Contact: natalie.gearin@muralarts.org or (215) 685-0750.
notes: The pages say 3 high school sites and 6 middle school sites on the enroll page but 16 sites in total on the page, so ask which site is near you. Mural Arts also has paid summer work experience through Career Connected Learning (see the C2L PHL card). Ask whether classes are free. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Twice a week. The fall session begins in late September 2026. The page gives no end date.
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the program pages. The page says students can later apply for scholarships, internships and jobs in the creative field.

who_can_apply: High school and college students. You must be able to go on weekdays for the whole program. You must live close enough to the museum to travel there each day.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how to apply. Contact the museum education team through the museum website.
notes: This is a small program. The 2023 press release said eight took part. It is part of the museum's African American Interpretive Program. Check the museum site for the next call for applications.
duration: 6 weeks, weekdays (the 2023 session ran July 5 to August 11)
pay_detail: The page says it is a paid six-week program. The pay amount is not stated. Public transportation help is offered.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the Youth Council page, which goes to pafa-museum.coursestorm.com. Each session has its own Register link.
notes: PAFA is on North Broad Street. The status is shown as open because the page lists a Register link for both sessions; the page gives no closing date.
duration: Fall 2026: Wednesdays Oct 21 to Dec 9, 4 to 6 pm. Spring 2027: Wednesdays Jan 27 to Apr 14, 4 to 6 pm.
pay_detail: Free to join. No pay or stipend is stated.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 or older to work as a city lifeguard; you can attend the screening at 15.
how_to_apply: Choose a pool and contact its supervisor, train with Aquatics staff to pass the screening, then finish the Red Cross certification and pre-employment steps. Contact: lifeguard@phila.gov.
notes: Free training is at Lincoln High School and Friends Select School. Pennsylvania's Department of Labor and Industry page says children need a work permit from their school district's issuing officer; workers under 16 also need a parent statement (Form LLC-75).
duration: June through August, about 35 hours a week; free training runs year-round
pay_detail: Starts at $16.85 per hour, about 35 hours a week from June through August. Red Cross certification is free for ages 16 to 24 who work at a Parks and Rec pool.

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 24. Residency is not stated on this page (the parent C2L-PHL program requires Philadelphia residency).
how_to_apply: Not described on this page; positions come through C2L-PHL. Questions: PPRC2L@phila.gov or 215-683-3683.
notes: Check the C2L-PHL listing for the actual application. The page had not been updated after Summer 2025. Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says work permits are required for minors under 18 hired to fill a position; the Parks and Rec page itself does not mention permits.
duration: Summer
pay_detail: Not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Students who live in Philadelphia. You must go to a Philadelphia public, Catholic, private or charter high school. You need a minimum GPA of 3.0.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply page on the program site when it opens in January 2027. You will need a high school transcript with fall 2026 grades. You need a 250 word essay about yourself and your interest in the program. You need an up to date vaccine record.
notes: The two pages word the grade rule differently (currently 9th or 10th on the apply page, entering 10th or 11th in fall 2027 on the main page); they describe the same group. Office: St. Leonard's Court, Suite 110, 3819 Chestnut Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104; contact form at https://vpse.upenn.edu/smp/contact-us/.
duration: Four weeks, on campus. Exact summer 2027 dates are not posted.
pay_detail: Cost and stipend are not stated on the program pages, so ask the program before you plan around either.

who_can_apply: Current 9th to 11th graders (Pre-College: 10th to 11th).
how_to_apply: Online application from the student: essays (400 words each), transcript, recommendations. For the scholarship, say you attend a School District of Philadelphia school and fill in the scholarship section.
notes: There are no scholarships for the Pre-College programs. Contact hsprogs@sas.upenn.edu or 215-746-2309.
duration: 2 to 6 weeks depending on program (2026 Academies: July 11 to August 1)
