pay_detail: 2026 tuition: 2-week Academy $6,700; 3-week Academy $10,050; Pre-College Residential $15,192 to $23,604; Pre-College Online $8,692 or $14,300; Online Seminars $2,950. $1,500 deposit and $100 application fee (waived for School District of Philadelphia applicants).

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 20 who want a law enforcement career. 14 year olds must be in high school. Under 18 needs a parent or guardian consent. Needs a passing behavior grade, good health for running and agility drills, and no arrests or convictions that would block a future police job.
how_to_apply: Use the online intake form on the program site. It is on the Apply and Forms page. If you are under 18, get a parent or guardian to say yes.
notes: Most cadets are not paid, but the pages do not say. Cadets who want to be police officers are urged to join the police recruit testing later. Other Explorer camps include a Pennsylvania State Police week and a camp at Fort Indiantown Gap. The program site lists a $50 a year fee for insurance and registration, collected if you are accepted. It also lists about $350 for probation uniforms.
duration: Every Saturday 10 am to 5 pm at the Philadelphia Police Academy, plus optional summer camps and a Washington DC trip.
pay_detail: Pay, stipend or fees are not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Middle school students in the School District of Philadelphia. They must go to one of the PYN school sites.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online forms in the PYN application portal. There are no paper applications. Send questions to afterschool@pyninc.org.
notes: For middle schoolers, so it suits younger teens. Pick a school site from the list on the page.
duration: School year (2026-27 sites are listed on the page)
pay_detail: Not stated; no cost is listed on the program page.

who_can_apply: Rising 11th or 12th graders enrolled at a PYN host high school, Martin Luther King High School or Simon Gratz High School. You must be able to come three days a week after school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Participant Interest Form on the PYN page. Questions: 267-502-3800.
notes: The page also lists a NextGen Career Club (Health Care).
duration: 3 days a week, 2 hours a session
pay_detail: Free career exposure program. The club itself is not described as paid.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 18, primarily rising 9th to 12th graders. The page does not state a residency rule.
how_to_apply: Use Apply Now or the interest form on the page (name, contact, current grade, cohort, three career fields). Phone 267-502-3800 or info@pyninc.org.
notes: About 400 internship slots a year across cohorts. The city's large summer jobs program is C2L-PHL, a separate application. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: 6 to 8 weeks per cohort (page also says experiences last 6 to 12 weeks)
pay_detail: Up to $1,500 for a 6 to 8 week experience, depending on hours and milestones

who_can_apply: The page says young people ages 16 to 24. Families and supporters can come too.
how_to_apply: Fill out the free pre-registration form on the event page (deadline Oct 15). Bring several copies of your resume.
notes: The page gives the day and month only; the year is taken from Oct 23 falling on a Friday in 2026. Under 16 is not listed as eligible.
duration: Friday Oct 23, 3 to 7 pm
pay_detail: Free to attend. The page says employers there have jobs and internships, but it does not say if they are paid.

who_can_apply: District high school students starting in 10th grade. Middle schoolers choose a CTE program on their School Selection application; high schoolers can join if their school has the program and space allows.
how_to_apply: Middle school: pick schools that offer your CTE program on the School Selection application. High school: talk to your school counselor.
notes: The page notes that students ages 14 to 17 need working papers to work. Which schools offer which programs is in the CTE Programs List.
duration: Typically 3 years, 1,080 hours of instruction; some programs 1 or 2 years
pay_detail: School program; the page does not say whether internships are paid.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. Positions are limited.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form on the camp page, including a one-page essay (why you want to volunteer as a CIT, experience with children, what you enjoy about nature).
notes: Camp is at 8480 Hagy's Mill Road, Philadelphia, PA 19128. The page's date line looks like a typo (June 15, 2025 to August 14, 2026), so confirm dates when the 2027 application posts.
duration: Two full weeks required; may be asked to work up to three weeks; one Saturday training in May
pay_detail: Volunteer program with no fee listed; hours can count as school or organization service hours.

who_can_apply: Clinic Support volunteers must be 16 or older (Animal Care requires 18+). Must attend a training session, sign the volunteer agreement and finish online ethics and safety courses.
how_to_apply: Complete the Wildlife Clinic volunteer Google Form. It is linked on the page.
notes: The general volunteer page says regular volunteers who work with children need Pennsylvania child abuse and criminal history clearances (free for volunteers).
duration: Minimum one 4-hour shift a week (about 20 hours a month)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students about to enter grade 11 or 12. You need a transcript, a list of activities and a personal statement of 250 to 500 words. You also need a recommendation from a teacher or counselor.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Add your transcript, a list of what you do outside class and a personal statement. Temple will email a form to your teacher or counselor. They use it to write about you.
notes: Finishing with a B or better can earn a Temple tuition grant of $1,000 a year for four years if you later enroll at Temple full time and keep a 3.0 GPA. Phone: (215) 204-7200.
duration: 4 weeks on campus
pay_detail: There is a program fee and optional housing. The cost page was blocked when read, so the amount is not confirmed here. Optional financial aid essay is on the application.

who_can_apply: Students in 9th or 10th grade at Philadelphia public district or charter high schools. They come from low-income families, or their parents do not have a bachelor degree, or both. They also plan to go to college. Five named schools get priority. They are Benjamin Franklin HS, Dobbins CTE, Gratz Mastery, Strawberry Mansion and The U School.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Send papers that show you are eligible, like a report card, test scores and proof of income. Then you have a virtual interview. Questions: 215-204-3636.
notes: Federally funded. You must have a goal of going to college. Income is not the only factor in who is accepted.
duration: Runs year-round, with a six-week summer program on campus.
pay_detail: Free to students. The program pages do not say if students get paid.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors, and incoming college freshmen. Needs a personal statement of 250 to 500 words.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Pre-College Summer Academy application online. Pick the Pre-College Summer Academy choice from the list. Add your personal statement to the form too.
notes: The page says that being accepted does not promise acceptance later at Villanova. It also does not give you an edge. A virtual info session is offered.
duration: 4 weeks in July
pay_detail: Residential $8,000 (room and meals). Non-residential $6,000. $2,000 deposit due at acceptance. $50 application fee.

who_can_apply: Students who are at least 16 by the program start date and have finished at least one high school science course. The program gives priority to students in the School District of Philadelphia. It strongly encourages Philadelphia high school students to apply. No grade level or residency rule is listed.
how_to_apply: Send an online application. It has a personal statement of one page, single spaced. It has two letters of recommendation. One from a science teacher is preferred. It has an unofficial transcript or list of classes with grades. Finalists have a 15 minute virtual interview in April. Participants and a parent or guardian go to a mandatory orientation in June.
notes: Contacts: Jason Diaz, 215-898-3803, jdiaz@wistar.org, or Cailey Bice, 215-898-3749, cbice@wistar.org. Absences of more than two days in a row cannot be accommodated. The stipend is not called a wage on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Four weeks (the 2026 session ran July 6 to July 30). An optional three week extension in August depends on funding.
pay_detail: $1,500 stipend for finishing the program, plus SEPTA passes for travel

who_can_apply: Any young person who is in a Philadelphia high school now will be considered. The program is for Philadelphia youth ages 12 to 24.
how_to_apply: Fill out the PYN youth interest form (Google form) and look at the opportunity list. Questions: 267-502-3800.
notes: PYN also runs a PYNtern program.
duration: 6 to 12 weeks per placement
pay_detail: $11 an hour starting wage, 120 paid hours split between classroom and job site.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 who live in Philadelphia. Any young person in a Philadelphia high school is considered. There is a preference for 12 named zip codes (19104, 19134, 19124, 19140, 19132, 19121, 19131, 19133, 19120, 19143, 19139, 19142).
how_to_apply: If a program provider already knows you, they send a link and referral code. If not, pick a provider from the map on the PYN page and email their recruiter.
notes: Spots are limited. A job is never promised. PYN suggests you email your chosen provider yourself with a short hello.
duration: 6 to 12 weeks per placement
pay_detail: $11 an hour starting wage, 120 paid hours.

who_can_apply: Philadelphia residents who are ages 12 to 24. You do not need to be in school.
how_to_apply: Visit a PA CareerLink center and ask for a Youth Navigator, or call 1-833-750-JOBS (5627). Philadelphia Works main office: 215-963-2100.
notes: This is a guide to programs, not one job. Also links the PHL Career Portal, apprenticeship search and the School District Opportunity Network.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Free help finding programs. Pay depends on the program you are matched with.

who_can_apply: The 2021 city announcement said Philadelphia residents ages 12 to 24. The current page does not repeat the age rule, so confirm it.
how_to_apply: Current page links a standing committee interest form (Formstack). Phone for the office: (215) 685-8307.
notes: City-wide teen council. The committee form on the current page is an interest form, not confirmed to be the membership application. Ask the office how members are chosen now.
duration: Ongoing; not stated.
pay_detail: Not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Email the zoo through the contact link on the volunteer page. No application link is listed.
notes: Separate options: Special Events volunteers (13+ for family events) apply through an online form; school groups of grades 9 to 12 can join Boo at the Zoo takeover shifts (those 2026 dates have passed). Docents must be 21+.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Piscataway residents only. Grades 6 to 12 and at least 12 years old; high school volunteers must be in grades 9 to 12 and at least 14. Must sign a Teen Volunteer Code of Conduct at training.
how_to_apply: High school: attend a library orientation session with a mandatory training video, then enroll if you meet requirements. Adopt-a-Shelf (grades 6 to 8): apply on the volunteering page when the session opens. Questions: teens@piscatawaylibrary.org (subject line Volunteer).
notes: Latecomers are not admitted to training sessions. Open only to Piscataway residents.
duration: Regularly scheduled volunteer hours after training
pay_detail: Unpaid; earns community service hours

who_can_apply: High school students ages 16 to 17 at two sites: Canonsburg Hospital and the Wexford Health + Wellness Pavilion.
how_to_apply: Fill out the AHN volunteer application (Apply Now on the volunteer opportunities page).
notes: Only these two AHN sites list a junior program for 16 and 17 year olds. Most other AHN volunteer roles are for adults. Check with the site for current openings.
duration: Wexford: Saturdays and in the summer. Canonsburg: not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older. You need a current lifeguard certification, or you can take the county course. A background check is required before a final offer.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Lifeguard Employment Application Packet and email it to lifeguards@alleghenycounty.us. Then sign up for a county course to get certified. If you already have a card, sign up for an aquatics test. Call 412-350-2455 with questions.
notes: The county lifeguard course is 2 days with the American Red Cross. It is for ages 15 and up. It costs $250 for residents and $312 for non-residents. You need a physical first. If you get certified through the county and work at least 225 hours at a county pool that season, the $250 fee can be paid back in full. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district.
duration: The full pool season. Exact start and end dates are not stated.
pay_detail: $16.00 to $18.00 an hour (listed for the summer of 2026)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18 who are entering 7th grade or higher in the fall.
how_to_apply: Register for the training on the nature camps page. Questions to Scott at sdetwiler@aswp.org.
notes: The 2026 training was held at Beechwood Farms Nature Reserve in Fox Chapel. The page does not mention 2027 dates. The page does not say whether ANTS are paid for service hours.
duration: One 4-hour training plus 30 hours of service during June and July day camps
pay_detail: Free to join. Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Teens at Club locations that offer Workforce Pathways: Carnegie, Estelle S. Campbell (Lawrenceville), Shadyside, Downtown and McKeesport. The page does not give an age range.
how_to_apply: Use the Returning Teen or New Teen registration link on the Workforce Pathways page. Or use Register Now at bgcwpa.org/registration. Financial assistance is available. See the Financial Assistance page. Phone: (412) 782-5710. Email: contact@bgcwpa.org.
notes: Confirm first: ages, cost, schedule and whether any work is paid are not on the pages. The Clubs also run two Club Teen Centers (Downtown and McKeesport).
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the program pages, and the page does not mention paid work. Financial assistance is available for Club membership.

who_can_apply: Natural History camps: teens 14 and older. Powdermill Nature Reserve camps: ages 14 to 19. Art museum camps: 16 and older. Each museum has its own application form.
how_to_apply: Use the museum's own teen camp volunteer application form. It is linked from the Carnegie Museums volunteer page. There is one form each for Natural History, Powdermill and Art. Questions: volunteers@carnegiemuseums.org or 412-353-4680.
notes: The apply link above is the Natural History form. The Art museum form is https://form.jotform.com/230685138792162 and the Powdermill form is https://form.jotform.com/230595011446148. The Natural History page also lists a Teen Advisory Board with an interest form (https://form.jotform.com/243505851081150); its ages are not stated. The Kamin Science Center teen volunteers are a separate card.
duration: Summer camp season. Hours and camp dates are not stated on the volunteer pages.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: At least 15 by June 6, 2026 (the 2026 posting). You must live in the City of Pittsburgh and hold current lifeguard, first aid, AED and CPR certificates. You must pass the Citiparks lifeguard performance exam and a background check.
how_to_apply: Fill out the City of Pittsburgh job application online. It is on governmentjobs.com. Then call the Citiparks Aquatics Office at (412) 323-7928. Ask them about test dates, classes and cards.
notes: The posting says applicants 18 and under with no high school diploma or GED must show a valid work permit before they are hired. It also needs Pennsylvania Act 153 clearance, fingerprints and a medical exam. The job number in 2026 was 26-LG1A-01.
duration: Part-time seasonal. Training starts in April; the end date is not stated.
pay_detail: $18.00 to $20.76 an hour (2026 posting)

who_can_apply: Cadets ages 12 to 18. The Pennsylvania Wing page lists Become a Cadet as ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: The squadron page links a Google Form for people interested in joining and the wing's Become a Cadet page. It lists no squadron email or phone. The Pennsylvania Wing headquarters can be reached at 717-220-3517 or hq@pawg.cap.gov.
notes: The Pennsylvania Wing lists other squadrons in the Pittsburgh area. They are Golden Triangle, Jimmy Stewart, Washington, Beaver Falls and Butler. Ask the wing which is closest to you. The dues range and first-year cost come from the national Civil Air Patrol cadet page.
duration: The squadron meets Tuesdays from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. at Baldwin High School, 4653 Clairton Blvd, Pittsburgh, PA 15236.
pay_detail: Civil Air Patrol says annual dues are $25 to $50 depending on location, and a fully active cadet may spend $300 to $600 in the first year (minus financial help). The squadron page does not state its own dues.

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 by the program start, in 10th grade when applying, and U.S. citizens or permanent residents with a green card. Meant for students who lack access or resources in computer science.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the CMU Pre-College application portal by February 1, 2027. Residential only; full participation required.
notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines are confirmed on the pages (the apply portal could not be read). Limited spots. The admission page lists two different dates for this application (February 1 and March 1, 2027); the page and the deadlines table both say February 1, 2027, so apply by then. Completers may be invited back to AI Scholars.
duration: 4 weeks, June 26 to July 24, 2027, residential
pay_detail: Fully funded: tuition, housing and meals are free; limited travel help for families with transportation barriers

who_can_apply: High school students at least 16 years old by June 26, 2027 who are in 10th or 11th grade when they apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the CMU Pre-College application portal. The scholarship option is only considered under the February 1, 2027 deadline.
notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines are confirmed on the pages (the apply portal could not be read). Expensive; shown so families know the cost and the scholarship route. The three fully funded programs (AI Scholars, CS Scholars, SAMS) cost nothing. Check the cost page again in November 2026 for 2027 prices.
duration: 3 to 6 weeks depending on the program (summer 2027 starts June 26)
pay_detail: 2026 prices ran from about $5,999 (3-week music, commuter) to $14,688 (summer session, residential, 2 courses), plus a $75 application fee and an $800 enrollment deposit. 2027 prices are posted in November 2026. Full scholarships for students with financial need.

who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old by the program start who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents and in 11th grade when they apply. The program focuses on students underrepresented in STEM.
how_to_apply: The application opening date is not posted; apply online through the CMU Pre-College application portal by February 1, 2027. Residential only; scholars must attend the full program.
notes: Status is unconfirmed only because the application opening date is not posted; the 2027 deadlines above are confirmed on the pages (the apply portal itself could not be read, it needs JavaScript). Competitive and limited spots. The page gives no application opening date. Scholars cannot take other summer programs that overlap. Questions: cmu-sams@andrew.cmu.edu.
duration: 6 weeks in person, June 26 to August 7, 2027, plus a short virtual jumpstart June 21 and 22, 2027
pay_detail: No cost to scholars beyond travel to and from Pittsburgh

who_can_apply: High school students (and college students thinking about transferring). No grade or age minimum is listed.
how_to_apply: Pick a date under 2027 Pharmacy Exploration Day on the page and use that date's registration link. Questions: Jason Stack, (412) 396-5182.
notes: Sign in 7:45 to 8:00 a.m. Drop-off and pickup are on Bluff Street behind Mellon Hall.
duration: One day, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
pay_detail: No fee is stated on the page. Lunch, an ice cream social and parking are free.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. No art or glass experience is needed. Scholarships are offered to all students.
how_to_apply: Click Register Now or the scholarship link on the Youth Programs page.
notes: Not a job. Included as an art skills program. Check the registration page for cost and dates.
duration: 10 weeks (beginner) or 12 weeks (advanced), once a week after school
pay_detail: Class fee not stated on the page. Scholarships offered to all students.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18 from surrounding neighborhoods. You must apply through Learn & Earn (Partner4Work).
how_to_apply: Apply to Learn & Earn at partner4work.org/learn-earn. Choose Homewood Children's Village as your group. Tell them you want to work at Grow Pittsburgh.
notes: Work sites: Shiloh Farm (7209 Thomas Blvd., 15206) and the Grow Pittsburgh office (6587 Hamilton Ave. #2W). The year includes a Garden Youth Summit (2026: July 30). The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district issuing officer.
duration: 6 weeks (2026: June 22 to Aug 7), Tuesday to Friday, 9 am to 3 pm
pay_detail: $12 an hour, 20 hours a week

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Must be at least 14 by the application deadline. Late applications are not considered.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application (or download one to email or mail) during the window. Selected teens are interviewed and must complete an orientation.
notes: Teens accepted twice a year (summer and school year). The next summer window should open in January; confirm on the page.
duration: Summer Teen Program and School Year Teen Program (hours per week not stated)
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: All youth ages 11 to 17. Pre-registration is required.
how_to_apply: Register online with the ticket link for each tour or call 412-237-3400. Call to join a waitlist if full. Cancel at least one week ahead.
notes: Tours are NOT at the science center. They are on-site at partner workplaces or on a virtual platform, and each listing gives its own address. Some tours need long pants, closed shoes and tied-back hair.
duration: One 2 to 3 hour tour (10 a.m. to noon for most)
pay_detail: Most tours are $15 per student. The page also says $13 in one place, so confirm at sign up. Need-based scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 19 per the meeting schedule section (the program overview says 10 to 19). A separate Tween L.E.A.D. is for ages 10 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up link on the Teen L.E.A.D. page. Contact Tonja Grate, tgrate@kingsleyassociation.org.
notes: The page does not state a current start date. Its examples are from 2024 and 2026, so confirm the program is running this year and where it meets.
duration: Mondays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, 4 to 6 p.m.
pay_detail: No cost to join. No pay stated.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 23 in Allegheny County and the City of Pittsburgh. Income and residency requirements apply (details on the application).
how_to_apply: Apply online through Partner4Work during the spring application window (new participants and returning participants use different links). A complete eligible application does not guarantee a placement, so apply early.
notes: Questions: summer@partner4work.org or (412) 932-2950. A separate Year-Round Learn & Earn (fall, winter, spring work sessions) serves ages 16 to 23 in the City of Pittsburgh but only for people who already finished a summer. The page does not mention a work permit; the Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says work permits are required for minors under 18, so ask your school or the program how to get one.
duration: Tier 1 and 2: June 22nd, 2026 - August 7th, 2026. Hours per week are not stated on the page.
pay_detail: Paid wages (hourly rate not stated on the program page)

who_can_apply: Anyone enrolled in high school (grades 9 to 12) in the greater Pittsburgh region. Teens fill out their own application.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It is linked from the museum page that asks for applicants. Applicants heard back in a few days. Send questions to Laurie Barnes, Education Director, at lbarnes@mattress.org.
notes: This is a high-commitment program: you are expected to come most Thursdays. The 2026-27 call was not found on the pages.The museum is at 509 Jacksonia St, Pittsburgh, PA 15212.
duration: Thursdays 4 to 6 pm, October to May, with a winter break (2025 to 2026 schedule)
pay_detail: Free to join. No pay or stipend is mentioned.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 interested in animal-related careers (age counted as of June 1, 2026 for the 2026 session). Must commit to at least 8 of the 10 days in the chosen session.
how_to_apply: Submit the volunteer application when it reopens, attend an in-person group interview, and attend orientation with a parent or guardian.
notes: Questions go to the volunteer contact on the National Aviary volunteer page.
duration: 10-day sessions; orientation with a parent or guardian in late May
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students who have finished 9th grade up to graduating seniors. No age limit is listed. You must be available for all program dates.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form (Apply Now link on the page). It has short essays. Interviews include the student and a parent or guardian.
notes: 2027 dates are not posted yet. The page also lists an overnight retreat in the Laurel Highlands. Phone: South Side Office 412-682-7275 (Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.). The page does not list a contact name or email.
duration: 5 weeks, Tuesday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
pay_detail: $1,200 stipend over the five weeks (2026). Also a raincoat, t-shirts, water bottle, work boots, bus passes and tuition.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 19 who have finished at least one year of high school. You pick one of two weekly groups (Wednesday or Thursday) and must attend all of the dates.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form on the Phipps page when the next group opens. Use the sign-up form on that page to be notified. Questions go to the high school programs coordinator at amule@phipps.conservatory.org or 412-622-6915 ext. 3804.
notes: The page lists two different dates for the final Youth Garden Summit, so confirm with Phipps. The stipend is not described as a job on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Seven-week course, one afternoon a week (12:30 to 4:30 p.m.) at Phipps, plus a Youth Garden Summit at the end
pay_detail: Free to join. Participants receive a stipend (amount not stated on the page).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who enjoy working with children. You must be able to get Pennsylvania Act 33/34 clearances. Phipps pays back the fees.
how_to_apply: The page says the first step for volunteers is to fill out an application. Accepted applicants then go to an interview, orientation and placement meetings. The page does not give a form just for teens. Email the volunteer coordinator listed on the Phipps volunteer page to ask. That is Deb Knorr, dknorr@phipps.conservatory.org.
notes: Confirm first. The volunteer page gives no teen deadline or teen form. Ask Phipps for the current age rule and dates before you plan around this.
duration: Summer camps held June to August. Hours are not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Clearance fees are reimbursed.

who_can_apply: Students from high schools in the Pittsburgh region who have completed one year of high school biology. The page does not state an age rule.
how_to_apply: The page says a link to the application will be posted when applications open. To get updates, join the email list by contacting Jess Robertson at jah99@pitt.edu. Questions: Dr. Becky Gonda, 412-383-5739, reg11@pitt.edu.
notes: No research experience is needed. Free PRT bus passes are available. The honorarium is not called a wage on the page. The page's dates (June 28 to July 16) are shorter than 'four weeks', so confirm the length. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Described as a four week summer program. Summer 2027 is tentatively June 28 to July 16, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
pay_detail: $1,000 honorarium, paid at the end of the program

who_can_apply: Current 10th or 11th graders at a high school in the Greater Pittsburgh area or Western PA. You need a strong interest in science and a GPA of 3.0 or above. You must finish a biology class by the end of the school year. You must commit to the full four weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. It has two essays of up to 200 words each. A high school teacher must complete the recommendation form. It is uploaded at the end of the application or emailed to phsa@pitt.edu by the deadline. Incomplete applications are not considered. Applicants are told by email in mid to late March. They confirm by April 1.
notes: The main page says public high schools in one place and all high schools in another, so ask which applies to you. The award is not called a wage on the page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Four weeks. The 2026 session ran June 22 to July 17, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Students who finish receive a $1,000 award at the end. Public transportation support to and from campus is provided, and transportation for field trips.

who_can_apply: Qualified high school sophomores, juniors and seniors. Students who are often left out are encouraged to apply. You must be at least 14 to live on campus. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Send the application on the page with at least two letters of support from counselors or teachers. If you are accepted, sign up and pay the $25 fee. Contact summercamps@pointpark.edu or 412-392-3456.
notes: Run with the National Association of Black Accountants (NABA). Residents must be in their rooms by 10 pm. The page showed the 2025 schedule.
duration: 1 week, residential only (2026: July 26 to 31)
pay_detail: Tuition is free for accepted students. A $25 non-refundable registration fee holds your spot. You pay your own travel to Pittsburgh.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12, or recent graduates. No experience needed. Residents must be at least 14 on the first day. Only the first 15 students who register and pay the deposit get in.
how_to_apply: Register online through CampDoc using the Register Here link on the camp page. Contact summercamps@pointpark.edu or 412-392-3456.
notes: Discounts: 30 percent off tuition for Point Park employees, alumni and immediate family, and $50 off for signing up more than one person or program. The schedule includes a firearm safety session. The schedule can change.
duration: 1 week. 2026 sessions: July 20 to 24 and July 27 to 31 (day or residential)
pay_detail: Tuition $700 plus $100 non-refundable registration fee ($800 commuter). Room and board adds $750 ($1,550 resident). Payment plans are available.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in the fall, and/or recent high school graduates. No age range is listed.
how_to_apply: Register at app.campdoc.com/register/pointpark and pay the $25 fee. Contact summercamps@pointpark.edu or 412-392-3456.
notes: Space is limited. In 2026 the page said housing for summer programs was full, so commuters were dropped off at Academic Hall, 201 Wood St. The page showed the 2025 schedule.
duration: 3 days (2026: June 29 to July 1), day or residential
pay_detail: Tuition is free (paid by the Rowland School of Business and sponsors). A $25 non-refundable registration fee holds your spot.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in the fall, and/or recent high school graduates. No age requirement is listed.
how_to_apply: Register at app.campdoc.com/register/pointpark and pay the $25 fee. Contact summercamps@pointpark.edu or 412-392-3456.
notes: Bring some cash for snacks and off-campus activities. The page showed the 2025 schedule. Instructor: Robert Derda, M.S.
duration: 3 days (2026: June 29 to July 1), day or residential
pay_detail: Tuition is free (paid by the Rowland School of Business and Brentwood Bank). A $25 non-refundable registration fee holds your spot.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. Crews are for teens ages 14 to 18 who want to join the summer program.
how_to_apply: The page does not say how to apply. It says to check back for openings and links to an SCA job board. Call Darren Gruetze, Pittsburgh Program Manager, at (412) 325-1854.
notes: Crews have two adult leaders age 21 or older. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry says minors under 18 need a work permit from their school district issuing officer; ask SCA or your school how to get one. Check the SCA page often because it shows no openings right now.
duration: Starts the last week of June and runs through the first week of August each year
pay_detail: Paid. The pay rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 17 (having turned 15 by June 1, 2026 for the 2026 program). Two non-relatives must complete a reference form. Needs proof of a negative TB test and a Tdap shot before orientation.
how_to_apply: Check the teen page in early January for how to submit an inquiry. Questions: chpvolunteer@chp.edu or 412-692-5185.
notes: Interviews are limited and selected by criteria. The volunteer office does not handle shadowing, internships or research requests; contact departments directly for those. Adult volunteer program is 18 and older.
duration: At least 8 weeks over the summer. The program page says two or three days a week (6 to 8 hours). Assignments page: one 3 or 4 hour shift a week.
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students in good school standing. You must be at least 15 at the program start for the computational sites (CompBio, COSBBI, Surgery). You must be at least 16 for the other sites. There is no residency rule, but out of region students must find their own housing.
how_to_apply: Send an online application. It has two short essays. It has one or two references, who get an email. It has a resume and a high school transcript. It has parent or guardian contact information with a digital signature. It also has your top research site choices. PDF files are preferred. In person students may need proof of vaccination.
notes: Very competitive. Another page describes it as an eight week program; the apply page says seven or eight weeks (June 14 to July 30, 2027). Questions: hillman.academy@pitt.edu or Steven Jones, 412-624-5904 (from the program's Oct 2025 profile). The stipend is not called a wage on the page. The apply page does not mention work permits, so check with the program before assuming one is needed.
duration: About seven weeks. Tentative 2027 dates: June 14 to July 30, 2027.
pay_detail: Free to attend. Stipends are offered to qualified students from a background underrepresented in biomedicine (details are on the stipend page linked from the application site).

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18 who commit to at least 9 workshops. Space is limited. (The Tech25 page says 13 to 18; the Warhol page says 14 to 18, so ask if you are 13.)
how_to_apply: Applications are closed. Watch the Warhol teens page and the Tech25 page for the next round. Questions: teens@warhol.org.
notes: The Warhol teens page says applications are closed. The Tech25 page says 'apply now!' but gives no dates. Ask Warhol before you assume it is open. The Warhol teens page also lists paid Student Assistant jobs at the museum. No ages or dates are stated. Email teens@warhol.org or see Carnegie Museums careers.
duration: 12 weeks, Mondays 4 to 6 pm (Print Lounge in The Pop District)
pay_detail: Free to join. Teens get a stipend for workshop sessions plus extra stipends for each performance. Amounts are not stated.

who_can_apply: Pittsburgh area teens ages 15 to 18 (high school students).
how_to_apply: Send in the online application by the deadline. Work samples are optional. Email teens@warhol.org with questions. Bus tickets are available for transportation.
notes: The 2026-27 deadline was 2026-10-09, so email teens@warhol.org to ask whether late applications are accepted. The Warhol also hires paid Student Assistants and runs a free Teen DJ Academy (ages 14 to 18, stipend) and School of Drag (ages 14 to 18); see the Teens page. Paid work for people under 18 in Pennsylvania needs a work permit. See permit.html?state=pa for the exact permit and steps.
duration: Weekly Thursdays 3:30 to 6 p.m., Oct 15, 2026 to May 2027
pay_detail: Participants receive stipends (amount not stated)

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 who are interested in animals and conservation (having turned 14 by June 1, 2026). Must commit to one day a week for at least 5 of the 7 weeks.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application when it opens. All applicants are interviewed in person before acceptance. Not all applicants are accepted.
notes: Volunteer role, so no pay. Contact the Volunteer Services Manager through the zoo volunteer page. The page's age requirement reads 'having turned 14 by June 1, 2026' even though it describes the 2027 program, so ask the zoo to confirm the age cutoff date. Confirm dates when applications open.
duration: 7 weeks, one day a week, 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. (June 15 to July 31, 2027)
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: The event page does not describe the application steps. Contact the zoo education or volunteer office, or watch the page for the next season.
notes: The Jan 23, 2027 session is on Zoom. Some sessions run 9:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. to fit field trips. The page lists no application steps or program-specific contact; the zoo's general phone is 412-665-3640.
duration: 13 sessions from Sept 26, 2026 to May 1, 2027, mostly 10 am to 12 pm, plus a May 1 all-day field trip
pay_detail: $25 program fee

who_can_apply: Teens in high school. Eligibility by town and grade is not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the crews page (rootsrising.org/apply). Questions: info@rootsrising.org, 413-344-0816.
notes: Market Crew is for Farm Crew graduates. Farm: 923 Barker Rd, Pittsfield.

pay_detail: Summer Farm Crew pays up to $2,000 for 5 weeks. Fall and Spring Farm Crews pay up to $800. Market Crew pays $15 per hour.

who_can_apply: Grades 9 to 12. Must live in Princeton or attend a Princeton high school, with an active library card in their own name.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application and a signed reference form. The papers were due Sept 4 at 5 pm in the 2026-27 year.
notes: Ask the library's teen staff if you have questions.
duration: October to June, first and third Tuesdays at 7 pm, one hour
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens going into grades 8 to 12 who have a Princeton Public Library card in their own name.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Give your library card number and a signed reference form. Spots for Maker Assistant and Program Intern are limited.
notes: The June 5 close date is from the page's 2026 cycle wording; confirm for 2027.
duration: At least 10 hours. Program Intern camps run in July and August. In the 2026 cycle, applicants heard back June 15.
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid. Verified service hours.

who_can_apply: Current high school students in grades 9-12 who live in the five boroughs, with parental consent and NYS working papers, and who register as library volunteers.
how_to_apply: Complete the Idea Submission questionnaire on the library volunteer site during a submission window. The Civic Engagement Team will contact you to get your idea library ready. Questions: volunteer@queenslibrary.org.
notes: A limited number of projects are accepted and a branch must agree to host. Other QPL pages list ages as 14-18 for this program, so check the age limit if you are 18.
duration: Varies by project
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn community service credit for time presenting.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17 with a signed parent consent form. The page says some projects do not require NYS working papers, so check each project's description. Students at schools outside the country or the state may use a waiver.
how_to_apply: Get the parent consent form and NYS working papers (from your high school office), create a volunteer account, search projects and click Express Interest/Sign Up, then interview and get an offer letter. Questions: volunteer@queenslibrary.org.
notes: Library says some projects do not need working papers, so check each listing. Working papers take 1-3 weeks from your school, so start early. They are issued regardless of immigration status. Under-14s can only volunteer with a parent or guardian.
duration: Varies by project
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteer hours count as community service credit.

who_can_apply: Generally ages 16 through 24. You must have a low income. You must meet citizenship or residency rules, or have other approved status. You must meet background rules. An Admissions Representative reads your application. This person decides if you can join.
how_to_apply: Create a MyJobCorps account on jobcorps.gov. Finish the application. Then an Admissions Representative sets up an interview. They review your documents and a background check. They also help you pick a campus.
notes: Mostly fits teens 16 and up who are out of school or want a different path. Housing: dorms are listed on the campus page. A center being listed on the Job Corps site does not prove it is enrolling right now, so confirm with an Admissions Representative. The training list above comes from the center's training page and may not be complete. Whether a state work permit applies was not checked.
duration: Not stated on the program pages
pay_detail: Free to students. The campus page lists furnished dorms, meals, basic medical care, books and supplies, and a living allowance paid in cash twice a month.

who_can_apply: At least 14 years old, or 16 for clinical units.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the program page. It opens the volunteer application site.
notes: The page does not show whether applications are open now, so check before applying.
duration: At least one 3 to 4 hour shift per week
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Rochester and Monroe County youth ages 14 to 20 in middle school, high school or a TASC (GED) program. College students cannot join. County residents outside the city must have a household income at or below 200 percent of the 2026-2027 poverty line.
how_to_apply: Apply through the ROC Youth Employment Network portal linked from the RochesterWorks page. You are matched with an employer. Extra applicants go on a waitlist.
notes: Also see ROC Your Job on the same site, a school-year paid program for ages 14 to 20 (not read in detail).
duration: 6 weeks (2026 dates: July 13 to August 21)
pay_detail: Paid. The wage is not stated on this page.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12 (2025-2026 school year rule).
how_to_apply: Online application with a 300 to 500 word essay on why you want to be a ZooTeen. Selected applicants go to a group interview and training.
notes: The zoo also lists a Wildlife Action Crew for ages 13 to 18. Questions: 585-336-7213. Need-based scholarships are available on request.
duration: 6 weeks from July to mid-August, at least 12 shifts
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens pay a $125 fee after being accepted. Need-based scholarships are available on request.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18 who live in Cumberland, Dauphin, Perry, Adams or York County, PA.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application, which is a Google Form. Then do an interview. Questions: hiring@leafprojectpa.org.
notes: 2026 season: June 22 to Aug 7, Monday to Thursday. Pay is $10 an hour, paid every other week. Applications for the 2026 season closed April 7.

pay_detail: $10 per hour (2026 season), paid every other week

who_can_apply: Teens 14 and older.
how_to_apply: Send in the volunteer application, online or at a branch. Add a note from your doctor and a form from a parent. Then go to the Teen Volunteer Orientation at your home branch.
notes: Dates for the orientation are on the events page of the library site.
duration: Summer reading season
pay_detail: Volunteer, unpaid

who_can_apply: Worcester teens ages 14 to 18. The page does not list other rules.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. REC runs an annual spring hiring process. Call REC at 508-799-9139 or check its Employment page.
notes: The pay rate and teen application steps are not stated on the page, so confirm with REC. Address: 108 Beacon Street, Worcester. The program employs up to 40 teens year-round.
duration: Year-round, with a 6-week summer intensive
pay_detail: Paid. The hourly wage is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Freshmen or sophomores at a Yonkers public high school. Academic merit is not a factor.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Add a recommendation form with two letters from a teacher, counselor, coach or mentor. Then do an interview with the Program Manager. Contact Pedro Betanzos at pbetanzos@hrm.org or 914-963-4550 ext. 219.
notes: Only for Yonkers public school students. The page gives the deadline as Wednesday in one spot and Friday in another. Oct 30, 2026 is a Friday, so confirm with the museum.
